title: Divine Administration
desc:
Gleb Radionovich exchanged confused looks with his (used-to-be) superior, Vladimir Leonidovich, who, like him, could not believe what he was hearing. Both are respected bureaucrats, lived and worked in Samara for many years. Of course, no one could sit in one place for so long without some dealings done behind the scenes, some money changing hands, in order to keep the whole thing going in an orderly fashion. 

Pavlov, who sat in front of them behind a simple desk, knew about it all. Every single person under them has personally begged him to help, as these crooks would rather be complicit in a crime like murder than to refuse a bribe, and raise wages even by a little. "Not only will you lose your position, henceforth you shall be prohibited from ever taking a job in this area of work. I will pray to our Lord that you can find a decent job. But I do not worry too much, after all, you and yours have quite the sum of money collected, no?" 

As Pavlov smiled, it was transparent to the two that they were finished here. "Stupid priestly vows...Who can live without wealth?! This bearded shit didn’t even blink when we offered a bribe." - Vladimir thought, as the two of them left, red as a tomato, and a guard closed the door. Pavlov sighs, "Not something I thought I would do as a priest. I like it though, heh."

title: God’s Gift
desc:
Morning service was proceeding as usual. Afanasiy was in his element, he loved reading the Bible, and even more so he loved reading it to his small, but pious flock. Church of the Intercession of the Holy Virgin was situated on a small hill, quite some distance away from most villages, yet still people loved coming here to hear Father Afanasiy’s sermon. 

After the service was concluded Afanasiy led his flock outside. He was surprised to see a different priest standing outside, guarded by a different priest, only that one was outfitted with combat gear. "Greetings Brother! You must be Father Afanasiy, a pleasure to meet you. I come bearing great news! You have been selected by our Elder, Father Pavlov, to be Custodian of St. Nicholas’s Cathedral. We are aware that you’re the only priest tending to this church here, but it is too remote, the patriarchate unfortunately cannot afford to upkeep it with such a meager turnout of people. God deserves better, you know!" He then let out a chuckle. 

Afanasiy didn’t know what to make of it, and while stunned like this, his flock was shooed away by the guard. Next thing he knows, he’s already escorted by these two men to a car. What of his small church? What of his flock? He didn’t know. He couldn’t know. He only hoped that he will do right by the people he will soon do service for, as he did for his previous flock.

title: A New Shelter
desc:
Five columns of people in ragged clothing stood before a building, which had a "Grand Opening" poster placed onto a wall next to the door. The people were cold, shimmying with their feet while trying to stand still and wait, nervous and somewhat excited. If the town cryers are to be believed, this unassuming house is a shelter, waiting to be opened. 

"I haven’t slept under a roof with four walls in years" - Ulyana thought, a middle-aged woman that looked far older than she is. "I hope I get a clean bed" - Fyodor thought, a young man who lost his home during one of the Nazi bombings. Their thoughts were cut short by the slightly late arrival of none other than the Patriarch himself. Arriving with a team of caretakers who would run the place, and a couple of guards of course, he walked with certain pride in his step. 

He finally stood before the doors, and, after taking out a key from his pocket, turned to the crowd with a small speech: "God’s faithful! I am here to deliver onto you - your just desserts. This is not the first community home I open, and it will not be the last! Amen!" After which he turned, unlocked the door in a swift motion of the key, and flung the doors open. "God, this never gets old" - Izvekov thought with a smirk.

title: A pillar of the community
desc:
Raheem is one of many citizens who want to make their community a better place. When he heard of an opening as a regional representative in his area, he told all his friends that he is going to apply. 

Raheem is a well-liked man, but there’s one thing which alienates him from everyone: He is a proud Muslim, thus seen as astray at best; and a national traitor at worst. Even so, his community is grateful to have him, even the most zealous Christians. So when he announces his goal, a lot of people are excited and promise to support him, as Raheem always has the peoples’ best interests at heart. 

One week later, he sits in the waiting room at the office where he applied. He and five other applicants received the most votes. Now it’s up to Izvekov to choose the winner. The interviews are already over. Raheem is excited, he feels it went well, even though Izvekov raised his eyebrow when Raheem told him he’s Muslim. 

The door opens with a creak. "His Holiness has decided." Izvekov steps out of the office and looks at every applicant. "First of all, I want to thank each and every one of you for applying for this job as a servant of god." He turns to face Raheem. "Mr. Amir, I concluded that you are the most eligible person for this job, especially with your reputation. However, I simply can not allow a heretic to hold this office. No matter how eligible you might be, it would be blasphemy to assign you. So I have to ask you to leave, and I will reveal my decision to the five other applicants." Izvekov faces the others, clearly not wanting to discuss this further.

title: A Momentous Occasion
desc:
Izvekov was new to technology, especially the one with wires and electronics. It kind of intimidated him, the sheer scale of radio equipment that was set up. It was all for a very important reason though. After days of preparation, most if not all cities’ main streets had a powerful transceiver and a plethora of megaphones. 

Having rehearsed the speech a couple of times, Izvekov checked the time. 12:00. It’s time. Stepping up to a fat metallic microphone, he spoke: 

"My fellow Russians. Father Izvekov speaking. We have come a long way since just a few years ago. Many of you would never imagine that this is where you would end up living, under the leadership of the army of Saint George, bringing Orthodoxy back to the importance level of a bygone era. Many of you dislike such a notion, it is no wonder, such a thing of the past must be unthinkable. 

Well listen to me now. Listen, for today marks the birth of the Russian Orthodox Republic! Not a nation that is archaic and fundamentalist, but one that is eager to evolve and change, go step in step with the modern world, and start a new, improved era for Christianity!"

title: The Choice
desc:
Tension hangs over the Order. The council has been talking for a few hours already. The most important choice in years is taken today. Who will lead the Order to godliness? 

Will it be Pavlov, the devoted scripture-lover, who wants to lead his People to a righteous, Bible-led state? 

Will it be the popular Izvekov, who plans to put Russia under an, albeit Christian, democracy led by godliness? 

Or will it be the righteous Antipin, who wants to fight heresy with a brutal fist? 

The decision will be made today. All three camps are nervous, and the people staying in pubs to distract themselves, or marching on the street in support to their favourite. 

Hours later, the head of the council finally steps out. Everyone waits with bated breath. 

"Good morning, fellow children of God. The council reached a verdict.

title: A New Prophecy
desc:
Hunched over his Bible, in a candlelit room, sits Pavlov. His entire focus is on the text, on his future if he becomes Patriarch. He seeks guidance in the Holy Text, a path forward, even a prophecy. 

Suddenly the door is flung open. His priest appears, out of breath: "Father! I apologize for the interruption - but the council has chosen you!" Pavlov looks up, taken aback, he stands up. "Truly?" Tears start forming in his eyes. He has been chosen to fulfill the Lord’s plans! 

Just hours later, he congregated in the middle of the town square with all his Followers and even non-believers who were interested to be converted. Holding the Bible tight to his heart, Pavlov emotionally preaches to the people. "My ascension under God will mark the beginning of a new prophecy - of a new age, the age of the benevolent Lord, the age of righteousness, the age of Life under Him!" 

He raises his arms above the crowd and sanctifies them briefly. Then he continues. "The days ahead will require hard work, but I know in my heart that if we just trust in God, we will overcome all obstacles that will be in our way. We will liberate Russia, and put it under God, as one nation once again! Glory to the Lord!" 

The people applauded loudly, some of them were crying. Pavlov smiles at them, shakes the hands of many attendees and then turns around to leave. But before he does, he leaves one of his personal Bibles on the floor for all to open and read.

title: A New Dawn
desc:
Hushed whispers wander across the council. Antipin stands before them, with a triumphant yet god fearing smile. All across the lands, celebrations in his name are held. But just as countless as them are the hearts stricken with fear. Will he bring about a reign of benevolent godliness? Or will he start off an iron-fisted crusade of his own? 

Uncertainty lies in the air, yet it is drowned out from all the cheering and laughing that Antipin’s followers loudly let out. Finally, after what seemed like an eternity, Antipin walks on the balcony to hold his first speech. 

"Servants of God!" 

The crowd watched him in bathed breath. "As you are all painfully aware, our motherland is poisoned by heathens. Not even our Order is safe! I thank all of you for your trust in me. I vow to you, our lands will be purged from all Satanist parasites and wicked devils. Those who truly follow God have nothing to fear. For all the ones, who want to destroy our benevolent work - You will not win! We have God on our side! Come out into the glory of the Lord, or be stricken down by His righteous fury!" 

A thunderous applause erupts. Antipin bows before his followers, quickly prays for them and walks back inside. As the people dance on the streets, Antipin has only one thing on his mind:

title: An Often Neglected Virtue
desc:
Slightly inebriated, Izvekov waltzes into his office. Another day of work, that, frankly, was getting way too monotonous for his liking. Sitting down in his chair, he decided to pull out a bottle from underneath the desk, holy water, to clear his head somewhat while the secretary is coming over with those damn papers needing signing. 

Not long after downing the bottle completely, the secretary, Nadya, comes in, and Izvekov notices the distinct lack of a mountain of paperwork. “Lord Above, is today my birthday? I can’t believe that there’s no papers!” - Izvekov chuckled. “Uhm, no, Father, I don’t think so. Today is a special problem that needs solving. I’m sure you’re aware of just how much poverty the warlords have left the people of Russia in.” Izvekov reclined in his chair and rubbed his temple a bit. - “Lord, yes.” - he sighed - “Give me some paper, please.” As Nadya is pulling a sheet from the middle of the long table, Izvekov is at the ready with a pen. 

Not bothering with giving this a title, Izvekov immediately outlines the points which need to be followed: /n1) Create a food kitchen in every district, those worked when we were a warlord ourselves. /n2) Start a public works campaign that pays small amounts of money, enough to get these people started. /n3)Build community homes in each major city, starting with Arkhangelsk, because it’s cold there. 

Signing the paper, Izvekov hands it back to Nadya, who smiles briefly and says:

title: A Chance For All Of Us
desc:
The prison cell that Andrei was held up in was crammed and dirty. Rats were running in it as the awful smell burned his nostrils, so much so that he almost couldn't breathe. The gray glued-together bricks gave off a paradoxical feeling of lifelessness, giving the ultimate implication that this was indeed, just a rest-stop towards the end itself. 

Fitting for someone like Andrei. A soldier of the Revolutionary Front having been captured during the so-called "biggest raid the Army of Saint George had ever conducted on the Red Army." He was not lucky enough to have been captured there and like many of his comrades before him, he was going to face the firing squad, before probably being condemned to Hell by the God he believed was not real. In either case, he lived a long bittersweet life and he was above all tired. 

At least he would finally be freed of his earthly shackles and see his family aga-. 

"Mr. Mikhailov." an calm but echoing voice came out of the hall, most prominent in his right ear. The lights revealed what Andrei would have mistaken for a Red Army officer if it wasn't for the badge of the Russian Orthodox Church on his sidearm, "The Patriarch has given you clemency. You will be transported out of this prison and into a rehabilitation center tomorrow." 

And before he knew it, the officer was gone. Only the same sight as before remained as he took in what his captor just said. Rehabilitation? Was this a trick? Or was he really getting spared? 

Regardless of how he felt, today Andrei would live, but whether or not that rehabilitation would be successful in the end is all up to him.

title: GAY.63.t
desc:
Kovalev remembered. He was marching through the Far East, the snow in his face, the Whites hidden in the forests as his men dutifully followed. He reported his friend, an Old Bolshevik, to the KGB as Bukharin tried to keep hold. He was there at Moscow, his bloodied palms on the rifle, waiting for the fascist scum to come. 

Kovalev remembered everything now, and it all suddenly felt so small. He saw all those people, killing, dying, vying, and suddenly all the ideological conditioning was gone. There were no Whites, Reds, Germans, or Russians. Only souls. 

And so when General Kovalev of the WRRF felt himself resurface, back into consciousness, the pull of his broken body dragging him back to reality, the agony felt like too much. 

“Well, this one is still alive.” Antipin stared at the crucified general, absentmindedly flipping the Scripture’s pages, “Let's begin.” 

They nailed them to the crosses at midnight, the mad Patriarch himself present to witness the Red Generals receive their punishment. But Antipin didn’t leave; he simply stared at the dying, his face lighting up with each cross going silent as the older and more infirm generals let out their last breaths. 

Now it was only Kovalev left. 

“God was merciful enough to let you die under his light.” Antipin grunted as he stood up, closing the Scripture and turning around to witness the sunrise, “Are you thankful?” 

Kovalev felt his vision darken as the first rays of sunlight hit his eyes, his chapped lips uttering one last phrase:

options.name: “Yes... I am...”

title: GAY.64.t
desc:
The chapel in the village close to Skythvkar was the center of Othodoxy for the village's inhabitants ever since it was built so long ago. It was far from the biggest, only a small building built in stone and bricks with the Orthodox cross laying above it. The small square windows, surrounded by wood, were the only sources of light for the inside, shining on the old oak pew chairs that sat next to the left and right sides of the building, leaving an opening in the middle. 

And that opening, that day, was used by an feverishly devoted visitor of the chapel. The committed man, religious to the bone and a readied servant to the Tsar, had used this chapel to refine his faith and to feel God's love on him. And tonight, he walked through the opening once more with the entire building empty of other visitors... except for one. 

"Sergey Vladimirovich Taboritsky." an young patriarch standing behind the sculpted cross said, "You have proven yourself to be a pious and faithful servant to the Holy Spirit. I therefore bless you of all your sins and invite you to join my cause." 

And Taboritsky, having finally walked up to the Patriarch, kneeled in front of him, on his face the expression of righteous servitude. 

"I will do as I must." he replied, "Thank you, Your Holliness." 

And Antipin could only look at his new accompinee, faithful and devoted to him in every possible way. He was the best servent he could ever ask for. 

And to think he wanted him dead back then.

title: A Divine Piece Of Paper
desc:
The rooms of the Patriarch's Palace were poorly dimmed and lighted. Only candles and small lightbulbs stood within the darkness that consumed everything else, as more and more snowflakes hit the windows that decorated the Palace, courtesy of the blizzard raging outside. 

And yet in the midst of it all, sitting in a room guarded by several guards in front of it, was the Patriarch himself, Pimen I. He sat on a chair with sweat dripping down his face and a black pen in his right hand, tapping against the wooden surface of the table with a piece of paper in front of him. 

That piece of paper served a purpose though. It was the written constitution of the new state Pimen would create. A state where the people will be both pious and free. Freedom under God. But Pimen was struggling to write the constitution in a way that would represent that ideal. To not give too much power to the church nor make the republic just another secular democracy. For that, Pimen toiled in his room, trying to make his dream come true. And after a while, he finally found it. 

"Article 4: Freedom of Speech is allowed so long as it does not offend God in a way that stands against moral values listed in the Old and New Testaments." 

And with hard work, the constitution was almost complete. It still had a few loopholes bit it was only a matter of time before they would be filled as well. With a sigh of relief, Izvekov simply laid on his chair after so much hard work, putting himself to a long, deserved sleep.

title: GAY.66.t
desc:
Pavlov sat in his office, reviewing foreign matters. Going over the documents, he realized just how little Orthodox countries he could consider for a potential friendship. Pretty much just Greece and Serbia, and only one of those has an active Patriarch of the Orthodox faith. Sighing, he called a secretary over, and asked for pen and paper. Even if it isn’t that beneficial, he wanted to align himself with the rest of the Orthodox world, so that it doesn’t fall apart any further. 

Receiving the tools, he began to write: 

“Greetings, fellow Patriarch of the holy Orthodox faith. I hope this letter finds you in good health. I write to you with but one goal in mind - unity. We both understand, that our faith, and our flock, is in dire straits - we are not as privileged and protected as Catholicism and the Pope in Rome, or as incumbent and spread out as Islam. Both of us remember that it was the Byzantine emperor that helped Tsar Vladimir convert Russia to the true faith. I hold this old friendship close to my heart, and hope to rekindle its flame in these awful times we live in.” 

“And so, let us join together, and bring the Orthodox faith back to being as tightly knit as it was before. Starting with this, we can hope to achieve great things, for us and our flock.”

title: GAY.67.t
desc:
Steven Barns paced in the New York City airport, checking his clock every two minutes. Being one of the very few government officials with good knowledge of Russian, he was extremely nervous to meet this particular guest. It was almost time. And, as if on cue, a plane was setting down. Steven rushed to the plane exit area, and waited for the guest of honor to arrive. 

Steadily walking out was a slim figure of Father Pavlov, curiously eyeing up the airport, followed by a tough looking bodyguard. He then noticed Steven waving at him, - “Welcome to America!” He said in English, after which he switched to Russian, - “I hope the flight was pleasant, if a bit long.” Seeing the nervously smiling man, Pavlov sighed, - “Yes, my good sir, it was. Now, would you please give me a tour of your city?” 

Not an hour later, they were on Broadway, walking on the sidewalk as the streets were packed with constantly honking taxis, garbage trucks, public transit and a few actual cars. Pavlov tried to distract himself from this incessant noise by sightseeing. Steven then stopped and pointed at a hot dog stand, - “Here is our city’s most valued food! Everyone loves hot dogs, you should try it!” Pavlov gave the stand two seconds of staring before saying, - “No, thanks.” Turning his head, he sees a boy counting pennies with a sad face, he clearly doesn’t have enough. Pavlov decisively turns and asks Steven to buy a hot dog. After it’s ready, he gives it to the boy, who gasps and says, - “Thank you Mister Beard!”

title: GAY.68.t
desc:
An inspection of the city, as routine as it gets, flanked by bodyguards, and only sticking to main streets. Pavlov did not enjoy his arrival to Samara. It hasn’t been a long time since these cities were home to enemies of our holy state, and as such he couldn’t appreciate them for what they are, instead having to be mindful of every corner, of a possible assassination attempt. 

Ironically, Pavlov was not expecting that, as he was going by an alleyway, a small figure ran out of it and into him. As the figure was tumbling backwards and falling flat, Pavlov noticed, after regaining footing, that it’s a really young girl, dirty from head to toe, and missing a shoe. She yells - “YOU STINKING MONK! BECAUSE OF YOU PEOPLE, MY PAPA AND MAMA ARE GONE!” Face red and eyes filling with tears, she stands up and throws a rock at Pavlov. Even though it hits him, a different kind of pain is terrorizing him from the inside. What “assassination attempt”? What “enemies of our holy state”? Did Pavlov actually forget that he was a man of God, that he used to read the Bible to children like her, teaching them the value of virtue? 

Snapping back to reality, Pavlov reflexively raises a hand, telling his bodyguards to stand down. He then kneels down to the sniveling girl, - “I am deeply sorry, I cannot bring your parents back. If it’s any consolation, know that they’re with God now, in Heaven.” He takes out 10 rubles from his pocket, and hands it out to her. Slowly, she takes it.

options.name: “God loves you, child. I hope you’ll understand.”

title: Bless My Gains Down In Gayny
desc:
Graphs, charts, numbers. Over and over again. Izvekov sat in his office, once again plagued with paperwork, this time even harder. But, ironically, today was Izvekov’s favorite day - he was dealing with the economy! Seeing the green line go up was one of his beloved activities as the Head of State. 

“Alright, so, from the top - integrating all of newly acquired land created a giant influx of GDP, glorious, the national debt is going down thanks to injecting our liquid reserves to pay it off, marvelous.” - Izvekov was mumbling to himself, he was in his element - watching money grow in amount, preferably in biblical proportions. All of it comes down to carefully managing expenses to create the most optimal GDP growth, all of it is directly tied to spending, but not spending too much. Taking a look at a graph there, overlooking a chart here, writing down the important numbers. Yes, over and over again. Thanks Vladdy-boy for that vodka distillery! Thanks Gutrum-fucko for those iron mines in Perm! Thanks Vlasov, you shriveled potato, for keeping the money you got from those deutchies! 

Chuckling, he reclined in his chair, and saw the sun going down. Sighing, he wrote down a couple more numbers and signed the extensive paperwork. He then stood up and started gathering the papers up in neat stacks. After he was done, he stepped out, and almost bumped into the secretary that was reaching for the door at the same time.

options.name: Smiling, Izvekov said to her: “Job’s done.”

title: The Pope? How Many Divisions Do We Both Have?
desc:
“Uh, what?” - Konstantin Katushev was puzzled by this question from Father Izvekov. “You know, Catholicism and Orthodoxy had a schism, a division. My knowledge on this is a bit rusty, so I was hoping you could enlighten me on how exactly to approach them. It makes sense to do so, if there is a chance to mend the schism, or at least be on friendly terms, then the Christian world would surely see us more favorably, no?” 

Konstantin blinked, - “U-huh. Well, to answer your question, other than this, and the Fourth Crusade, we didn’t really have any more “divisions”, so to speak. I assume you mean to write a letter to the Pope directly, as bizarre as that sounds?” Izvekov nodded with a smile, to which Konstantin sighed and pulled out his pen and readied a paper, - “Then by all means, speak.” 

“Kh-khm, my brother in Christ! Wait no, that’s too unofficial. Dear mister Pope! No that sounds stupid. Uhh, To the esteemed leader of the Catholic world! Yes, that’s good.” 

“To the esteemed leader of the Catholic world! /nThe Patriarch of Holy Russia greets you, as a fellow believer in God, Christ, and the Holy Spirit. Long have our people been deemed as separate, as though we are each others’ infidels. I say it’s time to dispel such notions! In these trying times, we, as leaders of our flock, need to come together and lead the faithful not as rivals, but as friends.”

title: GAY.71.t
desc:
The crowds gathered across the newly-made church in Sytkyvkar, tens of thousands of zealots and fanatics in and out of the building shouting the name of their Leader, waiting for him to arrive. And alas, he finally did. 

The crowd stood in silence as holy music started blaring across the church and the proud self-proclaimed warrior of Christ came on and started his sermon to his and God's people. His speech went on for about half an hour, becoming more and more unhinged along the way, yet it was at that moment, at the end, that the sermon became the most vigorous it had ever been before. 

„People of Russia!“ the Patriarch Peter II spoke, „I am here not only to speak to you but also the President and the people of the United States. Your nation is the most corrupt and decadent one that has ever bestowed this world. Your constitution and rights bestowed by it are a testament to the blasphemy of God that is ingrained in the core of your country. Indeed, Satan has helped you along with our immortal enemies to rise upon our dust to consume the world in sin. 

But do not worry, o people of Russia, I will swear on the behast of God and Christ to bring down this affront to the Holy Spirit down to the fiery depths of Hell where they belong, and when we deal with the Satanic Nazis and Japanese swine, you will be next. Death To America!!“ 

And the entire crowd all of a sudden burst into euphoria, rage and hatred, screaming endlessly and cursing for all its sin. Death To America became the slogan of the crowd who, once men and women, turned into rabid dogs, trained to destroy their enemies and to appease their master, not the Lord, but His servant instead, the Patriarch of All Russia.

options.name: „He is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble.“

title: GAY.72.t
desc:
""Since the dawn of the Earth, mankind has been constantly deceived and lied to by Satan and his legion of demons. Like pests, they have continued to do their master's bidding in spite of efforts by men to bring about Divine justice. And today, they now rule the world in sin as the so-called "superpowers." 

And such is the case for you, Fuhrer Martin Bormann. Your Satanic ideology has the German people as servants of Satan. Your degenerate brand of protestantism has no bounds in the amount of inhuman disgust it perpetuates on me. You are God and Christ's greatest enemy since the Romans and Judas. 

But do not think you can defeat us! You may be fooled by your large holdings of our sacred land that no one can neat you, but the might of our Orthodox faith and armies is great and unstoppable! We shall march to your land, kill anyone who dares to resist God's will, and burn Berlin to the ground. We shall cleanse your land like how God cleansed Sodom and Gomorrah, and we shall not leave anyone in your realm alive.""

Like pests, they have continued to do their master's bidding in spite of efforts by men to bring about Divine justice. And today, they now rule the world in sin as the so-called "superpowers." 

And such is the case for you, Fuhrer Martin Bormann. Your Satanic ideology has the German people as servants of Satan. Your degenerate brand of protestantism has no bounds in the amount of inhuman disgust it perpetuates on me. You are God and Christ's greatest enemy since the Romans and Judas. 

But do not think you can defeat us! You may be fooled by your large holdings of our sacred land that no one can neat you, but the might of our Orthodox faith and armies is great and unstoppable! We shall march to your land, kill anyone who dares to resist God's will, and burn Berlin to the ground. We shall cleanse your land like how God cleansed Sodom and Gomorrah, and we shall not leave anyone in your realm alive.""

title: GAY.73.t
desc:
""God gives his warriors salvation. Those who want fight for Him are the most blessed of all Othodox Christians out there, for they serve to spread His will and word to those corrupted by the Satanic leaders who deceive the population to become servents of the Devil. 

One such leader is you, Göring, and you are the worst of them all! You go conquering nation after nation after nation just so you can dwell in your degenerate homosexual values and sit atop your mountains of wealth with your never-ending greed fulfilled for just a short period of time. I feel no pity for the nations you have conquered, for they too far astray from God that they deserved death, but if you think you can conquer us, our great Godly nation, you are lying to yourself. 

Try it, try attacking us, and you will be met with might of God and our armies serving Him. Your protestant warriors will not take one foot of Othodox land without getting slaughtered. We will push you out of our nation and sack all of Germany as you and your sinful people suffer the Lord’s wrath. 

You will fall, we will prevail!"" 

And when the letter was sent to Germania and reached Göring, he only did one thing with it.

title: GAY.74.t
desc:
“There are many things the Devil has created in our day and age to convert Man back to his disgusting base ways, but you, Albert Speer, you must be welcomed in Hell as its best agent! 

Not only do you take the vile ways of Fascism, but you also embrace its most homosexual trends as you mix it with Liberalism! You and your Protestant agents march through Orthodox land, espousing freedom for its people while keeping them in chains! You cannot choose between sodomy and degeneracy, and so you take BOTH! 

This shall be our first and final warning, Speer! Let the Orthodox people go or face the Lord’s wrath along with your disgusting Germanic kind!” 

The Furher’s secretary re-read the letter, unsure of whether he should even pass it along.

title: GAY.75.t
desc:
In all honesty, the chances of this happening were so impossible it was borderline fantasy. In every other world, Patriarch Antipin would be writing letters railing delusional rants against the Satanic Germans, every Fuhrer would just dispose of the letter, not wanting to read a single word in it. 

But Fate was unpredictable, and God had other plans indeed. 

Fuhrer Heydrich, the Reichsfuhrer-SS and Butcher of Prague who had time and time again followed the orders of his superiors perfectly, had proved to be nothing more than a fool. That much was obvious, as the world watched as Germany collapsed underneath itself, ceasing to exist as a nation, the Thousand-Year Reich having lasted for nothing more than three decades. Hitler's death was followed by the scourge of God that was used to punish the nation for all its sins and everything it had done against the people of Europe and the world. 

But while the Americans and Japanese plotted to become the new masters of the burned-down remains of what was once Europe, Patriarch Antipin had his own plans. While in every other timeline, he would be writing letters to the Fuhrers of the German Reich, now he was planning with his military leaders a plan that would only commence one thing. Out of the ashes of Germany, Moscow shall be reclaimed, and a new Russia shall be born. 

And as for Germany and the suffering of the German people there, the Patriarch, his people, and the entire world in one way or another, all thought the same way:

options.name: ""Good riddence.""
options.text: ""Good riddence.""

title: GAY.76.t
desc:
Antipin stood in his office at the Patriarch's Palace, looking at a list full of names at his desk. This, however, was not an ordinary list. Rather, the names were those of people who betrayed their nation and God. Traitors, Satanists. All those who stood against him and Christ. And from scheming priests to godless communists, the list was very long indeed. 

He didn't have to worry about dealing with them alone though, because he had his trusty Minister of the Interior by his side. 

"First things first," said Taboritsky, wearing his iconic brown coat that he had every day, "We must deal with those traitors if we are to build a true Godly Russia!" 

"I agree." replied the Patriarch, continuing to stare at the paper in front of him, "All of them must be dealt swiftly. I think the logical solution should be to lock then up in prison camps. They will do a service to Christ for their sins there." 

Taboritsky, however, objected. "Nonsense! My apologies, Your Holiness, but these people are irredeemable!" he practically screamed in disgust and anger over the accused. He somewhat calmed down later so as to show respect to the Patriarch, but his tone still remained sharp. "They have betrayed God and Russia. The only just punishment for them is death!" 

Antipin simply remained silent, still sitting at his desk and looking at the same damn paper that was there before. Taboritsky had a point there, but do they really have to be this barbarous? Even if it was against heretics? Regardless, his time was up, and he had other work to do. Antipin thought about the topic of dissidents, and finally came up with what he had to say. Without warning, he looked at Taboritsky in the eye and said: 

"We'll talk about this later"

options.name: "Then death it shall be!"
options.text: "Then death it shall be!"

title: Cane Enable
desc:
Mylety Zykov felt tired, even the coffee cup he drank earlier didn’t help much. Most of last night he was busy drafting up plans, finalizing income charts, accounting in general, all because he was entirely certain that his dear Patriarch and leader of the Russian nation, Father Izvekov, was about as well versed in economy as a child, or a regular from the local pub. With a briefcase of neatly collected documentation in hand, he approached the office of said dear Patriarch. Yawning for one final time, he came up and knocked. 

No answer. Checking his clock, Zykov confirmed that at this time Izvekov should still be in his office. Knocking one more time, and receiving no answer, he opened the door, - “Apologies for the intrusion, but...” Zykov blinked. Izvekov was sitting in his chair, with his hands on his rotund belly, his mouth hanging open. He then snored, loudly. In front of him was a mess of papers, all covered in notes, scribbles, lines, etc. Zykov sighed, - “Good thing I came prepared.” 

Sitting on a chair at the side of the table, Zykov started to collect the papers on the table and arrange them accordingly, after checking on what they’re about. As he continued, he slowly realized - they were all paperwork for this month’s budget. And what absolutely stunned Zykov - it was all filled out perfectly! Not a single digit was something that would harm the economy, and he knew it wasn’t just lucky guessing, this is the work of a professional. After Zykov was done arranging papers, he sat up straight, thinking on what the hell would he even need to do here.

options.name: The work he pulled an all-nighter for, here it all was, already done by a snoring priest.

title: Suspicion Among Us
desc:
Another day, another group of priests in Gayny are causing a ruckus. Getting elected didn’t mean that everyone would respect the choice of the majority and would still resent you, sure, Izvekov was perfectly aware of that, but Dear Lord, would you guys just shut up already?! Thank the Lord that he was not hungover today, or else all this noise would do him in. 

Stepping out of his house, which was tightly guarded, for obvious reasons, he addressed his men and told them to follow him to that incessant crowd. A minute or so later, Izvekov got to them. He recognized most of the crowd as loyalists of Pavlov, and assumed the rest were those zealots Antipin hung around himself. “LORD ABOVE, STRIKE DOWN THE SCHEMING IMP, HEAR OUR PRAYERS, REMOVE THE CORRUPTION FROM OUR PIOUS LAND!” These chants were getting louder and angrier with each passing hour. Izvekov could not stand it anymore - “LOWER YOUR VOICES, YOU ARE BOTHERING OUR FLOCK WITH THESE INSANE RANTS!” Sure enough, they silenced themselves, but now the tension between the two groups was so palpable you could cut it with a knife. 

A man steps out, and slowly closes the distance to Izvekov with a weird smile, - “Dear Patriarch, how nice of you to join us. Father Antipin always said you were a reasonable person, so I hope we can come to an agreement.” He then extends his left arm, offering a handshake. Izvekov’s face went grim, “Only the Devil shakes on his left hand. God be merciful on your soul. GUARDS, FIRE!” Before the man could aim the gun in his right hand, several shots swatted the man down like a fly. The rest of the crowd quickly dispersed.

title: Emergency Meeting
desc:
Stepping into the impromptu court in the main church of Gayny, Antipin glared around, reflexively trying to intimidate people, only, not even a child would be intimidated by a weak, mentally sick man in cuffs. A part of the crowd wanted to raise their voices, heckle the rabble-rousing lunatic that was pushed forward by the guards to approach the judge, only, not even the most outraged individuals could find their voice when Father Izvekov was standing on the pulpit, overseeing the room with a stern and cold expression, unlike his usual jovial self. 

Passing through the nave and into the crossing, he stood before the judge, with a jury divided and placed into both transepts. Antipin knew that nobody in this place was on his side, none of these people were true believers, none of them loved and feared God like him. He made eye contact with Izvekov, the snake that is responsible for all of this. “The Lord will cast you down into Hell where you belong, you wretched heretic!” - Antipin exclaimed. Izvekov stared him down, - “Are those truly the words you want these people to remember you by? It is truly depressing to see someone lose any shred of dignity in this mad zealotry. The Lord is my witness - I did not wish for this to happen.” He then closed his eyes and let the judge begin: 

“Mikhail Antipin. You stand accused of treason, being behind an attempted murder, inciting discontent in both your fellow priests and followers, as well as misguiding our flock into a path paved by the Devil himself. I will now ask the jury for the verdict.” A moment filled with murmurs passes, after which a man stands up and says:

options.name: “Guilty.”
options.text: “Guilty.”

title: GAY.80.t
desc:
“What kind of madness is this?!” - An otherwise quiet evening was disrupted by the signature loud voice of Antipin. Only this time it wasn’t because he was preaching to his zealots. Pavlov stared at him, Antipin was reddening with rage. All Pavlov could think was - “Did I seriously not notice how my good friend became a rabid dog? Lord have mercy on our souls...” With a sigh, Pavlov responded - “This is the kind of thing that got us into this situation, Brother. You cannot seriously preach humility to your flock when you yourself cannot hold yourself together.” 

While the calm voice of Pavlov might have resonated with someone else, to Antipin, well, it just made him even more infuriated. All this “wisdom” and “reservedness”, all of it is malarkey! “Don’t call me Brother, your inaction will get the entirety of the good Russian people killed, not to mention the amount of snakes like Izvekov, who would sell their soul to the Hun, with absolutely no loyalty to anyone other than themselves! And what, you mean to cast me out, instead of traitors like him?! Preposterous!” 

Pavlov’s ears were starting to ring from all this shouting. He closed his eyes, and could almost recall the time, when the both of them were praying to the Lord above, united in one simple purpose - belief. Opening his eyes, that image was gone like dust, blown away by the fuming rant of an insane jingoist. Pavlov raised his hand, - “Enough. For the sake of our previous friendship, enough. Leave, I will not repeat myself.”

title: GAY.81.t
desc:
Cocks had rung out only a minute ago, yet Izvekov was already strutting down the street to meet Pavlov by the main church of Gayny. While he still had bitterness from failing at the vote (not being in charge really sucks), he at least knew for a fact that, unlike dear little Antipin, he was summoned by the Patriarch for a mutually beneficial reason, and that riled him up like free beer. 

Being near the church even before the first sunlight, Pavlov had gathered a, shall we say, group of “witnesses”, mostly consisting of those priests that supported Izvekov, and the flock that were advocating for his role as the Patriarch. Understandably, they were throwing side glances of contempt at Pavlov, like he was the town’s “special needs” kid, and not their Patriarch. At least this he could tolerate, at least they’re just bitter... 

Not a moment too late, Izvekov appears in full view of the crowd, which elicits cheers of acknowledgement. Pavlov looked at the crowd knowingly, then turned to the rapidly approaching Izvekov with an outstretched hand - “My good friend and Brother in our holy faith, Father Sergey Izvekov, it is a pleasure to see you in good health. I summoned you here for a very important reason - to offer you a position as a minister of economy in our new government, for the glory of Holy Russia. Do you accept it?” It took Izvekov only one moment of overlooking the crowd to realize what Pavlov was doing here, but... Argh, to hell with it!

options.name: “Of course Brother, I graciously accept!” - Izvekov said with a grin and a handshake.

title: An Unlikely, Yet Likely, Alliance
desc:
It was just another day for Izvekov. One would expect that the Patriarch's victory and conquest over Western Russia would embolden the man, flare his ego up a bit. While to an extent, it did, another side-effect of his victory over Western Russia was the ever-growing piles of paperwork to be completed by him every single day. And so for hour after hour, all Pimen II did besides sleeping, eating, and delivering sermons was rot and toil with his pen and papers, endlessly writing to the bitter end. 

It was a blessing for him, therefore, that during another one of his toiling missions, a guard went into his office and told him that a woman had asked to meet him personally, which he accepted out of kindness and personal relief over not having to write anything for just a minute. 

It was only when he saw who the woman really was, that face and cheekbones that showed a 60-year-old woman in a 40-year-old one, that he knew with whom he was really dealing with. 

"So, you are the Patriarch, aren't you?" asked the infamous Svetlana Stalina, daughter of a famous Old Bolshevik who fought with Bukharin for the throne. How ironic it was. 

"Yes." answered the Patriarch. 

"Good. I may disagree with your brand of democracy, but our differences are little compared to our shared will for freedom. I want to help you achieve your goals and make sure liberty thrives in Russia, and I belive you to be a capable man. Am I right?" 

Izvekov smiled, "I wouldn't stand here if I wasn't." 

"Quite the dry humour, fantastic. However, would you accept my aid? 

And with no hesitation, Pimen II simply looked at her, turning his head around to say:

options.name: „Yes“
options.text: „Yes“

title: GAY.83.t
desc:
“God, he’s so fucking fat!” - Not ones to mince words or attempt to be polite, Antipin’s zealots were busy dragging an unconscious body of Izvekov, face of whom was already filled with bruises. They were tempted to just throw his body down the church crypt’s stairs, but, sadly for them, Antipin ordered them to drag him there alive, so they couldn’t risk it. 

The crypt was filled with the stench of death - decomposing bodies everywhere, many of whom died in the last couple of months, during the numerous wars leading to reunification of Western Russia. A grizzly sight and smell, though none of it bothered Antipin, standing in the middle of it with a lamp and a pistol. As the grunts of his soldiers were getting closer, he reflexively squeezed the gun a couple of times, half excited to put an end to a terrible enemy of the Faith, half stressed out to be the one pulling the trigger. 

Finally, the bumbling, heaving zealots got Izvekov down, and set him in front of Antipin. He nodded to the bucket of water next to him, and one of the soldiers used it to splash Izvekov’s face. Coughing and yelling, Izvekov jolts awake, and is set up to his knees by the zealots. Izvekov only has a moment to realize where he is before Antipin says - “Prepare for your trip down to Hell, you scheming snake. May the devil be merciful with your soul.” Izvekov can only muster a “No, wait!..” before Antipin aims the gun at his head and pulls the trigger. As the lifeless body of Izvekov falls down, Antipin breathes a sigh of relief.

title: GAY.84.t
desc:
Early nighttime. Most, if not all, residents of Samara have huddled inside their homes, afraid to leave what little safety they still have. Patrolling soldiers of the Army of Saint George were like death brigades to them, it didn’t feel as though fellow Russians were the ones combing the streets for anyone suspicious, but German brigades of Dirlewanger. No way in hell soldiers can be so dead-set on finding at least a couple of unfortunate randoms, just to have someone to beat up, and still call themselves Russians. 

This day though, it held a special kind of cruelty. Zealots in the main square had simple gallows erected, for today will be the day of total executions of Samara leadership. “For the crime of betraying your nation, and selling out to the wicked Hun...” - Antipin stood in front of the gallows, eager to put these worms to the rope, and repeated the line he practiced, always the same for each and every person. Though he did start with the people in charge. 

Mylety Zykov already hung dead, eyes bulging out and mouth agape. Now it was Vlasov’s turn, who cried a little as the murderous preacher finished up his little speech - last moments were filled with utter regret to what kind of life Vlasov led. Snap, goes his neck. Bunyachenko was next, and rather than wait for Antipin, he just yelled obscenities at him for half a minute before Antipin ordered for his death. Oktan was the last of the “leadership”, and while he tried to buy his way out of this, Antipin was completely deaf to his offers of riches beyond imagination. Snap, goes his neck. Time for the rest of the filthy collaborators.

title: To Spread The Word Of God
desc:
Western Russia is finally united. With the blessing of God, our armies have conquered this region and freed our people from the suffering imposed by our enemies, domestic and foreign. It's not over for us, not by a long shot, but we have a chance, at least, to unite Russia once more and raise it to glory once again. 

But that doesn't mean our Godly crusade is limited to just Russia. All over the world, there are millions, billions of people who still do not see the light of the Lord. Who still live in ignorance of Christ and his ideals. It is something we, as servents of God, cannot ignore. 

While some countries refuse to be educated by our faith, others have welcomed our priests and preachers with open arms. Now, from the villages of India to the cities of America, they spread the word of Christ to the uneducated masses. They help the poor, the hungry and the needy. They do the Lord’s work in making the world a better place for all of us, and more and more people join us every day.

options.name: We shall only pray that such success continues in the future.

title: The Antichrist Reborn
desc:
The great church in Sytkyvkar was quiet, in spite of the thousands of people who attended it, because they came there only to listen to the wisdom of the Patriarch Pimen II. And he was speaking now, both in public and the newly introduced television cameras from the West, his wise words to the public and nation at large. 

"...And the Second Coming of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ will be preceded by the coming of His opposite. For Satan shall take up his abode in a man born to be the mockery and parody of the true Christ. Like our Lord, he will come to preach to the nations of the world, but he shall be possessed by the Devil himself. He will be the Deceiver, he will perform miracles and immoralities which have never been done since the age began. He will trick the world into believing he is above God, and with the help of his false teaching, his false miracles and displays of power, this evil man will offer to the world, a kind of earthly kingdom that is in everything the opposite of Jesus Christ’s Heavenly Kingdom, that will enslave and murder all those whom the Deceiver wants to enslave and murder.  

We must therefore, be vigilant, and have the faith necessary to reject the false teachings of the Satanic Antichrist. And in the Second Coming, as said in 2 Thess. 2:8, this “man of sin,” the “lawless one,” the Lord Jesus will “consume with the breath of His mouth and destroy with the brightness of His coming.”

options.name: May we have the faith to stand against him.
options.text: May we have the faith to stand against him.

title: GAY.87.t
desc:
The city of Gayny was not the biggest city in Western Russia for sure. Far from it. Prior to the establishment of the Orthodox rule it was nothing more than some rural settlement with some few thousand people living as its inhabitants. It was, for all intents and purposes, just some small town that stood just west of the great Ural Mountains that divided Europe and Asia. 

And yet, it went through so much. Whether it be because of German bombings, the refugees that settled there looking for compassion from God, or the wars that the state that town is in waged to unify all of Western Russia, it had become wholly unrecognizable from what it was during the era of the Bolsheviks. And now the city shall earn its reward for its perseverance, and finally become entombed in the history books for all time. 

"Your Holiness!" a young engineer wearing winter clothing came to Antipin, whose hands were clasped behind his back as he looked at the sight in front of them, "The cathedral is nearly complete! Only the dome remains to be built, and we are looking at the building being finished in the timespan of a month from now." 

In front of them stood the greatest cathedral the world had ever known. The gold-clad facade shone in the sunlight along with the snow that stood on the just completed parts of the roof and surrounded the building. The sheer size of the unfinished cathedral dwarfed every single other building that existed in its periphery and in the entire region, and the insides of the building were filled with murals of Christ and the Virgin Mary, and the Holy Trinity that created all that existed in the world. 

And Antipin smiled seeing it, for it was more than just a building. It was a monument dedicated to him, the Church he served in, and the greatest country the world had ever known. He was the Justinian Russia needed, and the cathedral was Russia's very own Hagia Sophia. And so he looked at the engineer and said:

options.name: "Excelent work, my child."
options.text: "Excelent work, my child."

title: GAY.88.t
desc:
Entry #112: Omsk 

Today, [?global.date.GetDateStringNoHourLong], was the day when I witnessed the result of being consumed by vengeance. What do people look like, when they live only to end the lives of those that wronged them and their loved ones. The Black League is an apt name - their people are those whose souls have gone black. Through hate. Through violence. Through indoctrination. 

Dmitry Yazov was most assuredly a broken man - with nothing left to live for but the accomplishment of his “Great Trial”, a mad idea, with an even madder execution. Our soldiers discovered his corpse a couple of days ago, while I was still on my way here. Suicide. Absolute insanity - to drive his people into becoming monsters, only to refuse being put to trial, and take his own life. As though he would suffer a worse fate than those he was “training” to become soldiers. 

You could see it in the city residents’ eyes - they desperately wished for our demise. We destroyed their “righteous mission”, we “betrayed Russia” by not being as genocidal as them. By not hating Germany as much as them. I will direct triple the amount of garrisoned soldiers here in the city and in the surrounding province, I cannot trust that these people would be complacent about our control. In time, I hope, people will learn to let go of their hatred.

options.name: And it made me wonder, if the Lord is afraid of his own creation...

title: GAY.89.t
desc:
Simo exhaled, his sniper shot hitting true, piercing the head of a clueless Russian like it was a watermelon. Although, even a truly experienced warrior could not escape his scope. Simo was praised as the White Death, racking up a kill count to rival that of a German machine gunner in World War 1. Even to this day, even after the Soviet Union collapsed, Russians still fall to the shot of his sniper rifle, evident by that guy who didn’t even bother to look around while scouting... 

“This was too easy, something’s not right.” - Simo thought to himself. Sure enough, he could hear the crunch of the snow - several others, buddies of the clueless guy, or were they? Doesn’t matter, Simo spots one of them, goose-stepping behind a fallen log. Not two seconds after, another shot. This time Simo didn’t manage to hit the head, the bullet had cut through the side of the guy’s face. Cursing something illegible, Simo switches weapons, he hears that the third guy is getting too close for comfort too fast, the KP/-31 SMG is for such cases. 

Scanning his proximity, Simo spots imprints going to a tree 12 meters from him. As if on cue, the Russian slithers out to shoot, only to get half the magazine of Simo’s SMG unloaded in his stomach, the rest spraying across the body. Choking on blood, the Russian falls, having not fired a shot. Simo sighs, and starts to reload his SMG, only then does he feel the gun pointed directly at the back of his head. “Gena is in heaven, and that fucker from the brazzerhud is in hell. Now it’s your turn to meet Lucifer, you monster.” The last gunshot of the day rings out.

title: GAY.90.t
desc:
From door to door, from house to house, that was the life of Alexei Ivanov now. To move like a rat, to escape the bloodthirsty cats killing anyone and everyone around them. 

Few had high hopes when the anti-communist Order arrived at Tyumen. They expected them to force confessions of loyalty to the church down their throats and bow down to the Orthodox Church, but the brutality that followed instead was unprecedented. The soldiers of the Order went from house to house and killed anyone suspected of being a communist. Women, men, young or old, that didn't matter to them at all. Like monsters, they slaughtered anyone in their path, and only the lucky ones and the traitors got away alive, or joined them side by side. 

And Alexei, being a proud member of the Communist Party, was an immediate target. 

BANG 

A headshot, going through Alexei's forehead as he tried to cross the street, was heard across all of Tyumen alongside all other fire that followed. His killer, a lone sniper stealthy hiding under a darkened window. 

And such a process repeated over and over again until there were no communists in Tyumen anymore.

title: A Godly celebration
desc:
Sounds of wine glasses clinking against each other echo in the hall. A large, decorated table stands in the middle of the enormous room, at the head of it a chair, so imposing as to resemble a throne. On it sits Sergey Mikhailovich Izvekov, the man of the hour. 

After years of fervent service to the one true God, he made it - he became patriarch. He raises his glass, filled with the holiest blood of all, takes a sip and says a silent prayer. This moment isn`t his - it’s the Lord`s. He closes his eyes, thinking of the journey behind him and all the trials he had to go through. Suddenly, he stands up and raises his arms: 

"Oh faithful servants of God, hear my words! I would like to raise a prayer to all the lost souls in this holiest of lands. To all the deceived minds, to all the enslaved bodies, to the holy, and to the sinful:All will receive their just and godly treatment in the Russia of God!" 

After a hushed prayer spoken by everyone in awe, he continues: 

"The coming years will be our greatest trial yet. But do not fear: We will prove our eternal servitude to the graceful God by overcoming it with faith in our hearts! God is on our side, we simply can not lose. So I ask you not to devote this moment to me. This isn’t my path, this is the Lord’s path. So when you think of today, don’t think of me, think of God!" 

As the room erupts in thunderous applause; cries, and shouts of "Praise the Lord!", Izvekov slowly sits down again. A smile appears on his face, filled with confidence that God truly will stand by his side, every step of the way.

title: A Deal With The Devil Himself
desc: With the establishment of the Order Of Saint George and God's Will across Western Russia, hope has arisen among the people of Russia that their country may be united again. However, in truth, it will take years before our government can take over the country and even more before we ready ourselves against the Germans if we do not fall by then, of course. That has, among other things, lead us to a dilemma regarding the state of our lands and foreign ambitions in Europe. Our people in the west, men, women, and children too, toil as slaves under the Satanic German dogs, breaking their backs and dying for the benefit of their masters and no one else. However, the masters can't serve alone. They also have their own dogs, our own people who have betrayed our nation to work under those who have enslaved and killed us. They deserve death for what they have done, yet now, unfortunately, we may need their help. Since these people value money over God and country, we too should adhere to the rules of their game. Buy them off and contact them. Some are probably working just to break the system from the inside when the time comes, but most of them will only join us when we buy them off with promises of luxury and power in our new Russia. With their help, our infiltrators will enjoy protection from above and our plan will easily commence when the time comes. Of course, we can just infiltrate the Reichskommisariats all on our own and hang the traitors on the gallows but it will be much harder to take on the Germans that way. The choice is hard either way. So what will we choose, our victory or our integrity?

A headshot, going through Alexei's forehead as he tried to cross the street, was heard across all of Tyumen alongside all other fire that followed. His killer, a lone sniper stealthy hiding under a darkened window. 

And such a process repeated over and over again until there were no communists in Tyumen anymore.

title: The Cost Of Sin
desc:
The smell of victory was so enticing to Izvekov. The victory over his former colleagues and enemies outside of his realm had begun engraving a sense of dangerous pride in him, thoughts of arrogance that would embolden him to do stupid things and hasten his own demise. But Izvekov was a humble man, and most certainly not an idiot. He knew how to do things well while also keeping his own morality in check. And it served him now, as he was walking in the Gayny prison with many unsavory individuals either staying silent, or shouting at him with swears and insults that didn't perturb him in the slightest. 

"Damn coward!" A young thirty-something year old man was screaming at the Patriarch as prison guards were carrying the thrashing maniac to the most nearby empty cell there was, "Your liberal friends will destroy Russia! God will punish you for your betrayal!!" 

Izvekov felt all sorts of things seeing the Antipin fanatic as he was finally pushed into and locked in his new home. Disgust at his ideology, relief at his guards who protected him, but most of all sadness for the man so lost in his thoughts and his path. But there was nothing to be done now. Only to walk forward.

options.name: *So he did, blocking out the insults the man hurled at him.*

title: Friends In Holy Places
desc:
“Wait, is this true? We’ll get weapons from the free parts of Russia?” - Gosha could barely contain his excitement after hearing the news from Yegor, as they were going down the stairs to the usual meeting spot of their small resistance group. “Yes, but I still don’t agree with this, Nadya said that they arrived from the insane zealot state across the Muscovy border. I know you guys are sick of hearing this, but socialism brought the church down for a reason - they exploited the poor, sat on a giant pile of money like dragons, which they receive from the state every month, and always worked against reforms. They are only an iota better than Nazis, if only that much.” 

“You’re preaching so much that you could be confused for a priest yourself, Yegor.” Opening the door to them was their impromptu leader - Nadya. Her older brother was the leader not too long ago, before he was found out. “Point me to a priest that would be advocating for leftist ideals and I will henceforth always read the Bible before going to bed.” Nadya smirked, - “True enough, but enough chit-chat.” 

Nadya turned to face a new face in the hideout - the person representing said zealots. At his feet were a few crates full of ammunition, leftover PPSh’s from the West Russian War, even a few grenades. A fat silver cross hanged from his neck, and although the glare from Yegor was anything but friendly, he gave them a big smile:

options.name: “By the Grace of Our Lord, Christ, the Almighty - I deliver you weapons of Holy Russia, with the intent to exterminate the Nazi Wyrm.”

title: Empath
desc:
“O God, whose mercies cannot be numbered: accept our prayers on behalf of thy servants, the downtrodden Russian people, and grant them an entrance into the land of light and joy, in the fellowship of thy saints; through Jesus Christ thy Son our Lord, who liveth and reigneth with thee and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen.” 

Reciting this prayer didn’t help, not even for the thousandth time, he still felt fake, a fraud. He wasn’t there to protect these people, couldn’t give anything, couldn’t heal their damaged bodies and souls… 

*Knock-Knock* 

“Father Pavlov, are you alright?” - the voice of one of his bodyguards snapped Pavlov out of his trance, - “You’ve been locked inside your chambers for hours, the men are just…” 

“I am fine! Yes, fine… I simply require solitude. Leave me, I will not stay here forever.” 

As the footsteps on the other side of the door receded, Pavlov slowly rose from his knees, peering around only to spot that damned report again. No, he knows what must be done now. Whatever time it must take, he will see to it that the German yoke on the Russian populace of Muscovy be broken…

options.text: …Forever.

title: Death Korps Of Voyna
desc:
“...Communist dissidents, or, in other words, enemies of Holy Russia and the True Faith, whose only aim is to obliterate the natural order of things and destroy the good old fashioned values upon which we used to rely…” - reading the orders sent by none other than the Patriarch-nutjob himself, Gavriil felt like all this preaching would kill him faster than a stray commie bullet would. A survivor of Auschwitz, he couldn’t care less what his leader was, what they wanted, or what they said. He just wanted to inflict pain that he felt in that hell onto others, hopefully getting to kill some Germans in the process. His little entourage of zealots in gas masks was far from the cold-blooded killer that he was, but at least they were eager. 

Some time later, in a dingy basement, Grigoriy and Rodion were busy making pipe bombs, - “Grisha, did you hear that Polina shanked one of those christ-fuckers in an alley yesterday? Can you believe that one of these holier-than-thou pricks actually tried to buy a hooker?” Laughter ensues, after which Grigory replied - “Well he was lucky that she killed him, and not infect him with AIDs or-” 

Door busts open, and a small object bounces into the room. Rodion can barely yell “Grenade!” when it erupts in the middle of the basement, right next to the pile of pipe bombs, creating a chain reaction that instantly kills them both. Outside, gas-masked soldiers finish rounding up the last of all the people still alive in the village. Not wasting any time, Gavriil does a mandatory “In the name of the Father,...” recital before blowing each of their heads with a shotgun, one by one.

options.name: Not an hour later, the whole village would be torched, completely wiped off the map.

title: Is This A Sisyphean Effort?
desc:
Terentiy Kravchenko Semyonovich, more commonly referred to as Semyonich by his colleagues, is one of the workers at the Vyatka Small Arms factory, one of the more hard-working workers in fact. While it was clear that he took joy in labor, the conditions set by the previously incumbent monarchist overlords were draconian, bordering on impossible. To add insult to injury - there were no rewards for his hard work, to the higher-ups he was only meeting their stupid criterias, nothing more. 

Terentiy was the last to expect that some priests over at Gayny would not only conquer Vyatka, but the entirety of Western Russia region. Even more unbelievable is that they chose a Patriarch that was a proponent of democracy. Although shocking, Terentiy still did not believe that a conservative Patriarch would do anything about labor laws. 

That was, until one day - Terentiy was working hard as usual, when suddenly a group of people he didn’t recognize came into the factory, led by none other than Patriarch Izvekov himself, who promptly started a speech: “Honest workers of the Republic! Today, in this factory, and all across our Holy nation, workers shall be recognised and justly rewarded for their monumental efforts done to preserve and improve our nation’s foundation, our skeleton! You there sir!” - He suddenly gestured for Terentiy to approach him - “I was told that you are this factory’s most dedicated worker,” - Terentiy slowly came forth - “You sir, are truly an example to us all! It would only be right to award you with premium, and I promise you sir -

title: The Woman Of Steel
desc:
Izvekov didn't think he would find many similarities in himself with Svetlana Stalina of all people. Their opposite religious views aside, she was the daughter of a communist who tried to vie for the red throne itself, and though she didn't get her father's political views, she did get from him his stubbornness and refusal to back down at any moment. 

There was a good reason this woman was known as the Woman of Steel, and it made Izvekov relieved that this was the end of their differences, and that only similarities followed from there. 

"And that is why we must be capable of arresting any proven fascist or communist opposed to our cause," Stalina rambled, just as she was doing five minutes prior, and she never stopped till now, "Any comments, Your Holiness." 

"Yes." the Patriarch nodded, "I agree with your goal, but does arrest and jailing seem too harsh for them? Perhaps rehabilitation should be considered a possibility for them." 

"Our democracy is still fragile." Stalina responded back, taking a cigarette from her pocket to light it and give herself a good smoke, "The enemies of it will do anything to destroy it and replace it with death and godless tyranny. I'm sorry, Your Holiness, but it's the only way." 

As much as he would try to deny it, the rational part of his brain told him that she was right in everything she said, because it was a matter of fact that they were stubborn in their beliefs and would overthrow the government before they could change their political views. At this hour, the most important one of the country's history, this was indeed the only way. And so he looked back up at Stalina's wrinkled face and said:

options.name: "You're right, then. We will discuss other matters later."
options.text: "You're right, then. We will discuss other matters later."

title: The Only Thing A Sinner Deserves
desc:
Antipin yawned as he was escorted across the burning ruins of Perm. It would be an understatement to say that the soldiers of the Order hated the Brotherhood and everything it stood for. Although Antipin himself resonated with said hatred, he was more so in contempt of the whole establishment, all he could think was “What a bunch of pathetic losers, Stockholm syndrome can’t even begin to explain how braindead this all was.” 

Coming up to a bunch of leftover Ari-shits left kneeling before a naked wall with bindings on, Antipin demanded from one of his entourage to give him a gun. Stepping up to the right-most captive, who was in the middle of crying, he started a monologue - “You know, all of this is just the fault of your insanely low intellect. If only you figured out that THINKING you’re superior DOESN’T actually make you superior, or God forbid, you would find somebody else to copy than the FUCKING NAZIS. But here we are.” *BANG* 

“All you guys are good for now is being left on the ground with a bullet in your head,” He moved to the next one, who was defiantly staring down Antipin - “either becoming food for scangers, or slowly fertilizing the ground” *BANG* “The Lord is my witness, you lot aren’t even worth being the dirt under Satan’s fingernails.” Moving up to the next one, Antipin noticed something weird about this sketchy bald guy, - “Hold on a fucking second.” Crouching in front of him, he grabs his face and takes a good look at him - “Well if isn’t the good Fyurer himself. Ha-ha-ha, you think becoming an actual baby-face skinhead would mean no one could recognize you? You’re the progenitor of all this chaos!” Standing up, Antipin orders two guards to lift him up.

options.name: “I won’t give you the satisfaction of a quick and painless death, imp!”

title: Cautiously Optimistic, Positively Excited
desc:
The sun was shining down the streets of Gayny, as the early afternoon air was as fresh as it could possibly be. As expected, many people were spending their time outside, though the atmosphere in the streets was nothing routine, with several groups of visibly happy people celebrating. Celebrating what exactly, you may ask? The inevitable reality of the young Republic’s total victory. 

Inside Izvekov’s same old office, the Patriarch was sitting in front of a few of his top generals and Konstantin Katushev, and while they recited the latest results, be it about the population of the Ural region, resources, or even the possible partisan movements from the remnants of their recently defeated enemies, Izvekov could only think about how unbelievable it all was. He was trying his hardest to hide his bewilderment that permeated him throughout the day, mostly through his eyebrows. And even though Katushev kept looking back to Izvekov while he was reading out civic reports, the man did not think much of it, mostly worrying if he was even delivering a good speech. 

As the reports were wrapping up, Izvekov used all his might to compose himself, and stood up to his men, and, after they were finished, he spoke out: “By the Lord’s Will, not mine, have we undergone this great test of Faith, and came out with a win. I thank you on behalf of our People, our Flock. And, while it is clear that not everything went as smooth as one might hope, one thing is clear -

title: The World God Only Knows
desc:
A convoy was making its way through the Sverdlovsk countryside. It wasn’t that long ago when this place was a battlefield, and it shows - craters dotting the fields, big and small, an undetonated artillery shell here and there, numerous vehicles blown up or left behind by the enemies. As smoke was rising from the recently captured city in their horizon and disappearing into the gray clouds, Pavlov was carefully observing the scenery, making sure to remember what it took to get where they are today. 

Arriving at the city center, a big hole in the city parliament was among the most noticeable things across the square. As soon as the vehicles stopped, Pavlov stepped outside, followed by the Order’s soldiers, who came out in droves from the personnel trucks, and, after getting the go-ahead from the Patriarch, moved on with the procedure. They would gather every citizen still left, and round them all up in the square, where the Patriarch patiently waited. 

After a couple of hours, most of the citizens were gathered, although some of them were roughed up for having resisted authority. Pavlov secretly winced at the sight, took a deep breath, and began: 

“Good people of Sverdlovsk! Do not be afraid! Let me start by officially welcoming thee as brethren people in this Holy Russia. The Lord brought us here today to deliver salvation - from the worst possible position that our people have found themselves in. It is, however, deeply regretful, that the good Russian people have allowed cruel ideologies and decadent ideals sow strife between ourselves. But no more! For while it is not the end of our current struggle, I implore thee, good people of Sverdlovsk, to accept the rule of God, and allow the Faith to guide everyone to glory. In the name of the Father, Son, and the Holy Spirit, amen!” 

No one in the crowd responded.

options.name: And though the air is not as tense as when the speech began, Pavlov felt a stone in his throat from the deafening silence.

title: Baptism by Fire
desc:
Within the Great Cathedral, Antipin waits as his followers fill in the large space. He surveys the cathedral and sees that all eyes are on him, except for his most loyal followers, who are praying in front of the altar. His followers eagerly await his important announcement. 

Antipin clears his throat, “My people! I come before thee to announce a vision given to me by our lord and savior Jesus Christ. As we all know, we live in troubling times and the world around us becomes more dangerous as time goes on. So, we sought new ways for protection.” 

The crowd became curious and they all talked amongst each other. Antipin paused and waited until everyone calmed down. 

“Yes, you all are wondering what I mean. We don’t need any sort of protection but from our very own lord and savior! But of course our lord and savior needs some support and that’s what our holy soldiers are for. But no I do not wish to unveil a new holy army, not a new law to govern our lands. No, it is something that will intimidate the world, including the German devils to the west!” 

Now the crowd was even more intrigued. What could it be? What does Antipin have in mind for the people’s protection? What could possibly scare the Germans who seem to be hellbent on exterminating the Russian people with extreme bloodlust? 

“My most loyal followers, I come before you to announce that our holy kingdom will commence its very own nuclear program!” 

It was silent at first, but suddenly cheers erupted from the people. Finally, the ultimate deterrent is going to become theirs soon. Their safety is now secured. 

“Yes, indeed! Soon we will harness the power of the atom, allowing us to purify our old Russian lands from the German filth and show the world our kingdom’s divine might! I challenge those German devils to step foot into our lands and be purified by a baptism of fire!” 

The crowd’s cheers were so loud, Antipin could feel the ground shaking beneath him. He motioned for the people to quiet down. 

“Yes, it is something that requires celebration. But, this process will take time and our safety and power is not guaranteed just yet. We are still feeble and weak against the sinners of the world. But I assure you, it will be done and our Kingdom shall rise onto the world stage and become a formidable power. Thank you, my most loyal followers and peace be with you” 

Antipin hurriedly walks off the stage. Soon, he will be able to wield the power of the atom for their holy crusade!
