“My most loyal followers, I come before you to announce that our holy kingdom will commence its very own nuclear program!” 

It was silent at first, but suddenly cheers erupted from the people. Finally, the ultimate deterrent is going to become theirs soon. Their safety is now secured. 

“Yes, indeed! Soon we will harness the power of the atom, allowing us to purify our old Russian lands from the German filth and show the world our kingdom’s divine might! I challenge those German devils to step foot into our lands and be purified by a baptism of fire!” 

The crowd’s cheers were so loud, Antipin could feel the ground shaking beneath him. He motioned for the people to quiet down. 

“Yes, it is something that requires celebration. But, this process will take time and our safety and power is not guaranteed just yet. We are still feeble and weak against the sinners of the world. But I assure you, it will be done and our Kingdom shall rise onto the world stage and become a formidable power. Thank you, my most loyal followers and peace be with you” 

Antipin hurriedly walks off the stage. Soon, he will be able to wield the power of the atom for their holy crusade!

title: How To Kill Your Devil
desc:
As time grew closer to late evening, and the sun shone its last lights for the day, the front yard of the church of Gayny was getting filled with cars, and out of each one came out at least one priest. Not wasting any time exchanging pleasantries with each other, mostly because no one in this crowd of priests was on good terms with the others, they all rushed inside the marble building. 

Pavlov was busy reviewing his notes in preparation for this inevitable discussion, standing behind a recently set up stand in front of the altar, as the aforementioned crowd poured into the building. Quickly skimming through the notes one last time, Pavlov looked up, and waited for the priests to gather. Movement eventually ceased, and the Patriarch raised his hands in a welcoming gesture: “Brothers! Fellow men of the Cloth! Praise the Lord for allowing this Conclave to gather!” A few of the priests responded: “Praise be!”, though most were silent. Pavlov lowered his hands on the stand: “I will get straight to the point - the reason for this Conclave gathering here today is-” 

“The Hun!” - someone in the crowd yelled out, which sent the priests into a bit of a disarray. A considerable number of the priests had jingoism to rival that of Antipin, visibly angry even being reminded of the Germans. Suddenly, a meek voice spoke out: “Must we really fight the Germans? How can we be sure that we could fight their war machine and emerge victorious, when so many had failed before?” Immediately, the first voice responded: “Spineless fool! Apathy is death! We need to act, before-”  

“Brothers!” - Pavlov raised his voice, silencing the noisy crowd - “It is deeply regrettable that this Conclave has split so heavily on this issue. I have no choice but to use my right as the Patriarch to rule on this decision… 

…We will not stand idle while there is a constant threat to the West, which not only occupies our land, but has us living in fear.

title: Indoctrination
desc:
It was a cold day today, a strong wind blowing through the compound with a slight snowfall. The cold bit Antipin’s skin but he was used to it. 

“ATTENTION!” A guard announces as Antipin walks into the compound. 

Antipin hears a loud clacking of boots as he walks in and he looks upon the crowd of fresh recruits in front of him. He thought they would show signs of distress from the cold or look at him with hatred. But they were disciplined, standing tall, eyes forward. All these young men, standing at attention, surprised him. These recruits, received from Western Siberia, were mostly made up of men from the Black League. He knew how hellbent and fanatical they were with destroying the Germans and reclaiming the old Russian lands. Some say they are purely fueled by hate. Because of this Antipin can't let his guard down. 

He walks through the rows, accompanied by two guards, and inspects his new recruits. Some of them were scrawny, like they were on the cusp of death. Antipin was sympathetic to them as he shared the same experience as they did, struggling for food and water. Some are tall and brawny. If they could, they could snap Antipin in two. Some just looked like they weren’t fit to fight. Either they looked overweight or underweight, they seemed like they couldn't even pick up a gun. Even then, he knew they were all capable of having bloodthirsty tendencies. 

Before Antipin left, he looked upon the crowd one last time. He knows some of them have their own unique struggles, which he wishes to solve. While some of them have their unique strengths, which he wishes to exploit. With that, he wishes to build a strong standing army deserving of unifying the Russian people in the eyes of God. As he leaves, he announces to the crowd…

title: No Room for Degeneracy
desc:
Antipin walks into the snow-covered forest. In the distance, he sees a flickering orange light, coming from torches for the coming ceremony. The snow on his feet starts to burn but he walks through the pain as he knows that Jesus Christ will protect him through every step of the way. He got to the clearing and in the center are people, standing in a circle. They all notice Antipin’s arrival and all of them bow to him as he walks through the small crowd. Within the crowd, are his most devout followers, kneeling and praying. While in the center of it all was a singular man and one of Antipin’s guards holding a torch. Antipin knew what that man had done, he was a rapist. 

He takes off his coat and starts to talk to the crowd, “My most loyal followers! Feast your eyes upon this sinful degenerate! Watch as the consequences of his actions be put upon him by the devil!” The crowd around Antipin cheered loudly, echoing through the forest which surrounds them. 

“PLEASE! PLEASE! I’LL DO ANYTHING! I’M SORRY, I WON’T DO IT AGAIN!” 

Antipin noticed the tears running down the man’s face. He had a small feeling of sympathy for the man, but he had to set an example for his people. “My loyal followers, do you hear him? Do you hear Satan pleading for his life? Do not be deceived by his falsehoods. If we let him free, he will repeat his sinful acts on other poor souls within our glorious kingdom!” 

His followers jeered and started throwing rocks at the man. Antipin’s guard shoots at the air to calm the crowd down. “PLEASE I AM SO COLD. HAVE MERCY!” 

Antipin looks at the man, “The sinner begs for mercy! Should he be given mercy?!” Cheers erupt from the crowd.“Then mercy shall be given!” 

He looks back at his guard holding the torch and nods his head. The guard then throws the torch onto the bonfire the man was standing on. It instantly combusted. The man’s screams could be heard for miles and Antipin stared at the inferno as it consumed the sinner until his screams were eventually quiet.

title: A Prayer For Peace
desc:
“Our Father, who are in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.” 

All the eyes in the cathedral were glued to the Patriarch, it is as though he was talking directly to them at this very moment. This kind of atmosphere could most definitely be attributed to the upcoming war. The final war of Russian reunification. And while most people felt the pull of the sermon due to this internal anxiety over the war, it is undeniable that a good portion of the people here genuinely believed. They prayed with him, not just listening, but taking the words to heart, to their very soul. 

It felt like forever since Pavlov was in his element like this - preaching the Good Word. He absolutely lost track of time, fully immersing himself in a passionate sermon: “...And Jesus called to him the multitude with his disciples, and said to them, ‘If any man would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me. For whoever would save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake and the Gospel’s will save it…” 

Doubts over his every decision that led him here, they were still in the back of his mind. They never left him, and probably never will, however it doesn’t matter. “So long as I can spread the Faith, let it touch the hearts and souls of good people, and let it spread even further, it will all be worth it in the end.”

options.name: This was all he ever wanted.
options.text: This was all he ever wanted.

title: In No Need For Cake
desc:
Fyodor Petrovich could probably be best described as a lower-middle class citizen. Living in a single bedroom apartment with his wife Ulyana, and two kids - Igor and Natasha, he lived a simple life of a warehouse worker. Wages might be a bit subpar compared to that of those that are in commanding positions, but he could feed his family, pay for the children’s education, and twice a year even get enough saved up to buy top quality meat and have a small feast for the household. 

One Sunday morning, Ulyana told him that they are running out of bread, and a few other things. Fyodor was a bit annoyed to have to spend money right now, as they were still a week away from the pay day, and he would have to use his savings for this. Nevertheless, he got dressed, kissed his wife goodbye, and went out into the busy streets. 

Cold early morning air hit him with full force, as unfortunately the wind just started to pick up right as he left the building. In this weather any stalls he usually frequented would not be open for business. Against his better judgment, Fyodor went to a grocery store that opened last month, much to the dismay of many vendors he bought produce from. In about half an hour he arrived, the concrete building of the store looked out of place next to the old rustic houses. Upon entering, he looked around - many different stands filled with produce, enough to make your head spin, and there's even a few stands of canned goods, and a couple of refrigerated stands with dairy products. Going over to the bread aisle first, Fyodor’s eyes almost went out of their sockets from shock - most of the bread on display was twice as cheap as the bread he bought from street vendors, and the rest was even cheaper! After composing himself, Fyodor took all the items he needed to buy and went to the cashier…

options.name: “That will be 40 roubles and 87 kopecks. Thank you, please come again.”

title: Our Just Reward
desc:
Fyodor Petrovich could probably be best described as a lower class citizen, someone that is seriously down on his luck. Barely scraping by, working as a barracks’ janitor, earning just enough money to not starve, living in a communal house without indoor heating with his wife Ulyana. Some days Fyodor wakes up to her wife crying - they had to give their kids over to the church because they weren’t able to provide for them, not since the change in regime. 

On a cold Sunday morning Fyodor stepped outside of his room to find most of his neighbors putting on their outerwear in a hurry. He asked his neighbor-friend Vlad what is the commotion for, to which he responds: “Haven’t you heard? The Patriarch has issued a relief program for the poorest citizens, the only real requirement is being Orthodox!” Vlad chuckled as he slipped himself into his jacket, - “You should hurry as well, who knows, you might miss out.” 

Fyodor wasted no time putting on his outerwear, quickly kissed his wife goodbye, and headed out with the small crowd. Outside the air was even colder, of course, but that did not hinder Fyodor as he went out of his way to get ahead of the crowd, almost breaking into a run at one point, but finally spotting a giant line in the distance. His heart sinking, Fyodor resigned himself and took his place in the line. After what felt like forever, Fyodor was finally in sight of his goal - two priests were handing out sacks to those in front, guarded by no less than four soldiers in full combat gear. The sacks were not large, they were all the same, and worst of all - they were running out. Fyodor was anxious, it might be that he was standing in the line for nothing… 

But finally, his turn arrived, the priest quickly looked Fyodor over, and handed a sack to him. Carefully taking it, he hurried back home, and once he arrived, he opened it with his wife…

title: For Whom Does The Bell Toll?
desc:
Father Afanasiy was still mulling over the assignment letter when they got within viewing distance of their destination. “How am I supposed to oversee this convention when I know next to nothing about politics? What do they expect a man of the Cloth to-” Afanasiy, train of thought is cut short by his car stopping. He finally broke his stare from the assignment paper and looked out the window - he arrived. 

Upon entering the room, Afanasiy was hit with an incredibly stale smell, as well as loud yelling coming from all around him - the discussion was already in progress. A few seconds later they noticed that the doors opened, and quieted down - “Ah, good Father, apologies, some of us were a bit too eager, and couldn’t wait a little bit before blabbing on about things they don’t understand-” A well dressed man addressed Afanasiy before being cut short by a person in simple clothes: “I will tolerate no such slander! You clearly provoked-” Afanasiy finally got to his seat and raised his voice: “I implore thee to calm thyself! It is unbecoming of good Christians to be at each other’s throats.” 

“Now, to confirm the topic of conversation, is it correct that this is regarding the matter of death penalty?” Some clear their throat, some cough, most people nod their heads, after which the well dressed man speaks: “Indeed Father. And it is imperative that we institute it as a viable legal decision when dealing with any criminals, so that-” The man in simple clothes cuts him off yet again: “How dare you mock the sacrifice of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ! He received a cruel punishment and took it in order to absolve humanity of their sins!” The well dressed man scoffed: “Oh how rich, equating every murderer and rapist to Jesus, you immature imbecile!”

options.name: Soon after the room was once again as loud as before. Afanasiy could not get a word in, and after a while only prayed that they run out of breath soon.

title: Divine Retribution
desc:
AFTER ACTION REPORT: 

An outpost was found near our border with the Reichskommissariat and to prevent any future German plans in raiding our Kingdom, I tasked my battalion with raiding the outpost. 

The outpost had three guard towers with German guards manning each one. Each tower allowed the outpost to have a 360 degree view of its perimeter. So, we planned on attacking at night. There was also a German convoy that came in every few hours, probably bringing in more supplies, which we can assume that the outpost is fairly new. The walls were luckily made with logs and sticks which made it easier to find an entrance into the outpost. We were going to take everything they had from guns to their food while also leaving no prisoners as the German devils didn’t deserve mercy. 

My battalion prepared for the attack at 1800 hours, setting up a forward operating base. They then attacked at 2400. Under the cover of night, they snuck through the brush and had the element of surprise. My battalion vastly outnumbered the German devils, 3 of ours to 1 of theirs. The raid lasted for about thirty minutes. It was a bloody battle but it eventually led to a major victory. We looted the armory and their kitchen. After that we rounded up the rest of the Germans who surrendered and executed them via firing squad. 

When we finished our raid, everything was utterly destroyed, buildings were on fire and corpses of the German devils littered the outpost. This operation was a major success and I wish to serve the Kingdom of Christ a lot more in the future.

title: Letting The Holy Father Cook
desc:
Kostya never was one with much interest in spiritual things. When his beloved mother died in a Nazi air raid a few years ago he could care less for whether she went to Heaven or not, he was simply devastated over the loss, a sentiment that is most prevalent in recent days. So when his dad suddenly brought him over to a church on a Sunday, months after Vologda was taken over by the Orthodox priests, it was clear that he was not thrilled to be there. 

Despite the initial dislike, Kostya was calmed by the smell of burning candles everywhere, and the overall warmth of the place. Incidentally, the Patriarch himself has come here to give a sermon. Seems like this is the reason for his father suddenly bringing him here, Kostya thought. Seeing as there’s nothing much better to do, he listened… 

“O God of spirits and of all flesh, Who hast trampled down death and overthrown the Devil, and given life to Thy world, do Thou, the same Lord, give rest to the souls of Thy departed servants in a place of brightness, a place of refreshment, a place of repose, where all sickness, sighing, and sorrow have fled away. Pardon every transgression which they have committed, whether by word or deed or thought. For Thou art a good God and lovest mankind; because there is no man who lives yet does not sin, for Thou only art without sin, Thy righteousness is to all eternity, and Thy word is truth. 

For Thou are the Resurrection, the Life, and the Repose of Thy servants who have fallen asleep, O Christ our God, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, together with Thy Father, who is from everlasting, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever unto ages of ages. Amen.”

options.name: By the end of the sermon, Kostya was bawling his eyes out, desperately hoping that his mom made it safely to heaven.
options.text: By the end of the sermon, Kostya was bawling his eyes out, desperately hoping that his mom made it safely to heaven.

description:
Kostya never was one with much interest in spiritual things. When his beloved mother died in a Nazi air raid a few years ago he could care less for whether she went to Heaven or not, he was simply devastated over the loss, a sentiment that is most prevalent in recent days. So when his dad suddenly brought him over to a church on a Sunday, months after Vologda was taken over by the Orthodox priests, it was clear that he was not thrilled to be there. 

Despite the initial dislike, Kostya was calmed by the smell of burning candles everywhere, and the overall warmth of the place. Incidentally, the Patriarch himself has come here to give a sermon. Seems like this is the reason for his father suddenly bringing him here, Kostya thought. Seeing as there’s nothing much better to do, he listened… 

“O God of spirits and of all flesh, Who hast trampled down death and overthrown the Devil, and given life to Thy world, do Thou, the same Lord, give rest to the souls of Thy departed servants in a place of brightness, a place of refreshment, a place of repose, where all sickness, sighing, and sorrow have fled away. Pardon every transgression which they have committed, whether by word or deed or thought. For Thou art a good God and lovest mankind; because there is no man who lives yet does not sin, for Thou only art without sin, Thy righteousness is to all eternity, and Thy word is truth. 

For Thou are the Resurrection, the Life, and the Repose of Thy servants who have fallen asleep, O Christ our God, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, together with Thy Father, who is from everlasting, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever unto ages of ages. Amen.”

title: How Good is a Shepherd, if He Loses His Lambs?
desc:
Antipin overlooks a company of soldiers, all in mourning. Some shed tears while others stared far into the sky. Their commander treated them like kings and his skill on the battlefield was unmatched by any other commander they knew and he led them through countless victories. Is anyone even worthy enough to replace their beloved commander? Does anyone even compare to him? Antipin knew how they felt and he wanted to give them their right of revenge. But he knew they wouldn't be able to fight in their current state. Antipin clears his throat and all eyes are on him. 

“My holy crusaders! I stand before you today to mourn our beloved commander Morozov. Slain by the German devils. He was a man, blessed by God with numerous talents. Especially his talent on the battlefield. You all know this. He was blessed with the gift of sympathy, something that is not common in these times. You all know this. But most importantly, he was a determined soldier, who was ready to sacrifice himself in the name of the lord! He knew the price we ALL have to pay on our holy crusade! I hope you all know, even in death, Commander Morozov is still with us, watching over us, leading us as he did during his time with us!” 

The mood of the crowd suddenly rose. Some were cheering and some were raising their weapons into the air. 

“Do not let his death be in vain. Let his skill in leading pass on to you all. Let his sympathetic nature pass on to you all. Lastly, let his inextinguishable fervor pass on to you all. Let me repeat once more, do not let his death be in vain! Now, my holy crusaders! This is your chance for enacting revenge for our Commander Morozov! A German camp lies just North of here! What say you? Should the German devils get what is coming to them?!” /n.nCheers erupted from the crowd. Bottles and weapons rose to the air. “Hm. May God have mercy upon their wretched souls. To battle!” 

The men charged towards the small German fort, weakly fortified and soon there was nothing left but a pile of ash.

title: The Gun Is Your Friend
desc:
Gleb, a fresh recruit from Vyatka countryside, only ever had experience with guns in the form of his cranky neighbor Tikhon, who would always chase Gleb off with his Mosin rifle whenever the young lad went into his garden to steal something growing there. He never imagined that a very similar rifle could end up in his hands, and he’d be expected to use it against people. 

Although getting used to this would prove to be quite the struggle, he took solace in knowing that he isn’t the only one with no prior experience in this - he quickly made friends with Grigoriy, Sasha, and Ilya, his bunkmates, and pretty much inseparable comrades, even in training. Today’s drill was finally one to be excited about - a shooting range. An hour ago Gleb overheard some fellows in the barracks saying that this whole training regiment was engineered by an American sergeant, and so Gleb secretly wanted to show that Russians can easily clear any challenges, especially those from Yanks. 

While all he was taught up until that point was “how to clean the gun”, from watching Tikhon aim and shoot at birds pecking at his apples he had some inkling of an understanding about the real thing. “Private Zamyakin! Forward!” Gleb was finally called up to the range, and he walked up to the sandbags, - “Take aim!” He places the gun roughly how he remembers it was placed, secretly praying that it won’t dislocate anything, - “Ready!” He breathes in and out a couple of times, then takes a deep breath, - “Fire!”

title: Celebration of the Baptism of Christ
desc:
There are many occasions to celebrate the Son of God, Jesus Christ, throughout the year for his followers, but the Baptism of Jesus is one of the most important events to commemorate the Beloved Son of the Lord. This wasn’t the first time Pavlov has held a sermon over one of the most important events in the life of Jesus Christ on this Earth, but that doesn't mean it's any less special to him, his soldiers that will reclaim Russia for God, and any of his congregation here in Gayny. 

“On this fateful day, nearly 2000 years ago, the Lamb of God was baptised by John the Forerunner.” Pavlov began, as he started his sermon to his congregation. Almost the entire town showed up to his sermon. Many did it as a form of escapism. From the German bombing runs, to the Famines to the constant bandit attacks near Gayny, there are many things to fear, so they must remember what they believe in even as the country they once knew has fallen apart if they want to see another day. “John believed he was unworthy of baptising the Son of God, ‘I have need to be baptised of Thee, and comest Thou to me?’ he said to Jesus, but Jesus simply said ‘Suffer it to be so now, for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness’. Jesus wanted John to set an example to the people and fulfil everything within the eye of the Lord”. Almost the entire church was listening to Pavlov’s words. They’ve heard this sermon before, many times in fact, but in this day and age, they cling onto the old traditions and the Order of Saint George. 

“Once the Baptism was finished, a bright light shone from the Heavens, the spirit of the Father of Christ descended as the spirit of a dove, saying ‘This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased’”. Jesus’s Baptism reminded Pavlov of when he started the Order. The Baptism was the start of Christ's mission to spread his word and the word of God. Pavlov remembered when he was taken in by the people of Gayny after the Great Patriotic War, when he saw a vision sent by the Lord. That was when he decided to start the Order of Saint George. He is certainly no Jesus, but he will be a loyal follower of him.

title: Horrific, Petrifying, White
desc:
Constantly looking over his shoulder, always going with the crowd, making sure to check around every corner - paranoia has taken over Anatoliy. Last month it was his co-workers and secret comrades - Evgeniy, Irina, Boris, Anna and Pavel. Last week it was his brother Oleg, his uncle Konstantin and his closest friend Nikolay. All of them have disappeared without a trace. Of course, nobody paid any mind to the disappearances, in fear of becoming the target. Everyone in the town knew what it was at this point, everyone had the name of this secret hunt on their lips, yet none dared to say it… 

Anatoliy peeked around a corner of the alley, and froze. There they were - clad in black and white combat gear, balaclava masks covering their faces, and with a shiny golden cross emblem on their shoulders. Antipin’s dogs. And it seems that they’ve gotten another victim, who Anatoly recognizes, and it gives him cold sweat - Prokhor, the (now former) leader of their secret group. Anatoliy stops looking into the alley and runs into the direction he came from - “How? When? Did someone snitch? I cannot believe this, they came after him, and now they’re gonna go after me! Oh my god!” - Thought Anatoliy, as he rushed across the emptying street back to his home. He cannot stay there, he has to collect his things and move, somewhere, anywhere. 

Dry heaving his way up the fifth flight of stairs, Anatoliy finally comes to his floor, only to fall to his knees when he looked up, and saw similar looking men to those that took Prokhor - “Ah, greetings “comrade”. We were wondering where you were, so nice of you to come straight to us.” Before Anatoliy mutters a single word, someone puts a bag over his head.

title: The fruits of our labors
desc:
Outside the window, a warm, drizzling rain was pouring, washing away all evil spirits, dirt and similar impurities from the Russian land. It hasn't been that long since the damned German pigs finished destroying and bombarding the holy land.In the window of the Patriarch's Palace, only a faint lamp light shone, reminding that someone was in it. 

At the table, in his typical work attire, Antipin was sitting and slowly sorting through the reports, reports and denunciations that had come to him today.Having dealt with the little things, he finally found what he needed: five reports...the main reports - on the state of the army, economy, garrisons, population, foreign policy, intelligence and promotion of the true Christian religion on the Russian land - recaptured from the remnants of the Boche, demons, apostates and other rabble, not worth the attention of God. 

"Come here, Sergey, they brought something nice here." Antipin said, now raising and lowering his eyes to the documents, then to Taboritsky sitting opposite him on the chair. Sergey rubbed his hands in anticipation and stood up, straightening his favorite fur coat. "What's Mikhail doing there?" Sergey asked cheerfully, heading to the table to see what his friend wanted to show. 

"Reports have come, Seryozha, on the most important topics." looking at Taboritsky, Mikhail said. 

"How many infidels have we destroyed for the good of God this year?" having already approached the table, Sergey began to peer into the papers, looking for relevant information. 

"Oh, Sergey, is that all you care about?" Antipin raised an eyebrow questioningly. 

Taboritsky laughed. "Well, of course not, we just liberated so many territories of Holy Russia, they are probably full of traitors." 

The Patriarch nodded, "Sergei, you're right, traitors to the word of God, as well as devils in human form, are a dime a dozen. 

These two sat and looked at the reports for a long time, laughing and rejoicing in their victories, rejoicing in the state of the army, the increase in the quality of life of the Russian people, rejoicing in the increase in industry...They rejoiced at the slow but faithful unification of Russia under God, those who have always protected the Russians… For when Russia will be united again... God's punishment will befall every German woman, child and man...

title: A Rifle for every Warrior, and a Revolver in every Holster
desc:
Five hundred rifles in just 2 weeks. Now that was something Commander Malinovski could be proud of. He remembers the days when he was lucky to get fifty rifles in a month. Niko smiled as he threw his left arm over Ioann’s shoulder. “Ioann, you know how to make God happy, I remember the days when we just had enough rifles to equip my platoon, now we’re able to fit an entire army and still have some of them leftover” Niko said to the delivery man. 

“What can I say Niko, all the boys in the factory want our country back, and that attitude is how we can make so many guns for your men” Ioann replied as he finished unloading the last crate of rifles from his truck. He remembers when the only guns he could get were from small workshops in Gayny. Now he’s delivering guns from everywhere. Refurbished Soviet rifles from Kazan, officer revolvers from Perm, grenades from Samara, hell he even got a new delivery truck from Vyatka. Things were really looking up for the Kingdom of Christ 

“You know what, I say we treat ourselves, least we can do before I head east” Niko suggested as he walked over to a storage room. Not long after he came back out with a crate of Vodka. “Here we go, the finest Vodka Vyatka has to offer, definitely much better now that the stupid monarchist is gone” Niko said as he grabbed two bottles of vodka, handing one to Ioann, which he gladly accepted. “How about a toast? To really make it special” Ioann suggested as he opened his bottle. “How about to Russia? Or the People? Or God?” Niko shook his head. “No, how about we toast the man who got us to where we are now?” Ioann gave a nod of approval. “I can drink to that”. Both men raised their bottles in the air…

title: Mending The Schism
desc:
Evening was setting in, as Pavlov retreated to his private chambers. Used to be that he had to light a lamp, or even just candles, and use those for light, but now the entire building has electricity, with lightbulbs lighting the way, as well as his room. As he stepped in, the first thing he saw was a small heap of letters on his desk. Pavlov sighed in exasperation, although he did ask to not be disturbed today people still needed important things from him, hence the letters. 

Resigning himself, he sat down before his desk, and skimmed through the letters. Conversion requests, letters about resistance to said conversion, an invitation to a church opening, ministers asking to sign some papers, with a fat stack of papers under the desk… 

Pavlov’s weary eyes almost missed it, but among them was a letter he could not simply ignore. He rubbed his forehead, and double-checked the sender: His Holiness, the Pope of Rome. Carefully, he opened the letter: 

“Honored Russian Patriarch of the Orthodox branch of our hallowed Christian Faith. 

I pray this letter finds you in good health, for we all find ourselves in grim and uncertain times. I am sure you understand why I write this letter to you now, - the world is more hostile than ever to the Good Word of the Bible, and the honest faithful in general. I, for one, have been utterly surrounded by the spiteful malignancy that is Fascism, and still see its hold over many people in Italy, and most of Europe. It is for this reason, and so many more, that the Christian world must come together as one! Sects of our Church mean nothing when the followers of the Crooked Cross eliminate all who do not revere it. ‘Tis blasphemy, I say!..” 

The letter did not end there, but Pavlov already pulled out parchment and a pen.

options.name: Overjoyed, he wrote a long-winded response letter that basically said: “YES!”

title: A New Kind Of Baptism
desc:
“What you hold right now is one of the cornerstones of our military - the Kalashnikov automatic rifle. Feel the weight! Its bullets can pierce through thin walls, be that concrete, stone, wood, especially wood! Several times in fact, if it’s some cover made out of wood! And all that power will most assuredly make you fall flat on your backs if you don’t grip and hold this beast tighter than a lion! While the German peashooters can hit a watermelon from 100 meters, the AK can blow it to smithereens from just 5 meters!..” 

Private Nikita stood in the second row from the instructor, who waved around the AK with one hand like it was nothing, while Nikita himself could scarcely hold the thing without his hands shaking, all while standing at attention. A highschool graduate from Onega, he thought his life would not amount much to anything as he moved around the country that took over his used-to-be homeland. After living as a farmhand down in Bashkiria for over a year, seeing the patrolling soldiers every once in a while, and soaking in their lively fervor as they passed by his field, well, something stirred inside him, and led him here, where he slowly adjusts to holding the weighty rifle. 

“...At first most of you will most likely not be quick to reload the weapon in such a manner, fumble a magazine and drop it - and it can result in your death! Especially if you are careless enough to bend over like a woman while the enemy takes his aim at your head! Alright, I will need one of you to come forward, see if you lot are taking my lecture to heart. Private Isayev, to me!” Nikita jerked forward, as if puppetered over to the instructor, - “Now, show “the class” how to reload the AK!” In a blind effort to prove himself, Nikita got the magazine out in a hurry, but dropped the rifle as he lost his careful stance.

options.name: A facepalm and a sigh later, the silence was broken by the instructor, - “At least the rifle wasn’t loaded. NOW PICK IT BACK UP, PRIVATE!”

After living as a farmhand down in Bashkiria for over a year, seeing the patrolling soldiers every once in a while, and soaking in their lively fervor as they passed by his field, well, something stirred inside him, and led him here, where he slowly adjusts to holding the weighty rifle. 

“...At first most of you will most likely not be quick to reload the weapon in such a manner, fumble a magazine and drop it - and it can result in your death! Especially if you are careless enough to bend over like a woman while the enemy takes his aim at your head! Alright, I will need one of you to come forward, see if you lot are taking my lecture to heart. Private Isayev, to me!” Nikita jerked forward, as if puppetered over to the instructor, - “Now, show “the class” how to reload the AK!” In a blind effort to prove himself, Nikita got the magazine out in a hurry, but dropped the rifle as he lost his careful stance.

title: How To Expand The Lord’s Coin Purse
desc:
“We’ll do it by committee, according to well-established rules that I, and many others, adhere to. I absolutely will NOT have you oversee the economy on your lonesome, are we clear, Brother Izvekov?” - these words from Pavlov sent the Patriarch and Izvekov into an intense staring contest. It was short-lived however, as Izvekov really didn’t want to deal with what he saw as a stubborn mule, - “Understood, Brother. But still, I want this “committee” to come together as soon as possible, we really cannot delay this matter!” Pavlov slowly nodded in response, with a sigh: “Yes, we shall send out the summons, it must gather in no more than a week.” 

As if no time had passed between then and now, Pavlov and Izvekov now find themselves a week later, locked in another staring contest, now in a big conference room full of suited individuals from all over the country, who now wonder why they’re even here. One short haired individual in the middle of the table slowly raised his hand and said what everyone but the two priests wanted to say: “...Excuse me, can we move on to the budget discussion?” Pavlov and Izvekov both broke their stares at the same time and looked at this daredevil of a person. 

Gulping audibly, he lowered his hand and continued: “It’s just that we began this meeting an hour ago, and ever since Father Izvekov proposed his plans for the economy, well, we couldn’t exactly get a word in, or even propose anything in return…” Izvekov rubbed his temples, and Pavlov clutched his beard, both in frustration, at the sheer ridiculousness of this situation. The good Patriarch now understood that this was all pointless - he only made everyone waste their time. Therefore he broke the silence first, and shocked everyone, even Izvekov:

options.name: “My apologies everyone for making you come all this way, but today we will simply be using Father Izvekov’s plans.”

title: Delivery for the Armed Forces of God
desc:
Fifty Rifles, just enough to finally outfit the entire platoon, thought Lieutenant Niko Malinovski, quality could certainly be better, but he’ll take what he can get. The platoon had God on their side, they were loyal to their core to their creator, but that's not worth anything if they had to fight with only sticks and shovels. Since this platoon was created, they lacked the critical gear to defeat the traitors and degenerates surrounding them. He turned to the delivery driver, who had just dropped off the crates of newly created rifles. “At least we finally got them. Glad to see the men at the factory are working as hard as us.” 

“Well, hard work can only get you so far” Ioann replied to Niko as he opened one of the rifle-filled crates. “Sadly we just don't have enough workshops or resources to make everything we need.” 

“Don’t worry my friend” Niko said as he grabbed some of the new rifles and laid them on the table “Soon we won’t be restricted to the factories here in Gayny, soon all the great cities and abundant workshops and endless piles of materials will be in our hands to give to God.” Niko smiled as he finished his sentence. Samara, Kazan, Perm. All these cities were within their sight, within the Patriarch's sight.

title: God’s Love And Mercy
desc:
Sergey Mikhailovich Kuznetsov, someone who grew up in a life of crime, orphaned at a young age, he had to fend for himself, stealing from the elderly and women, other children, and, after growing up, from alcoholic men too drunk to fight back. Not that fights never happened, with other criminals for random scraps, or even those he stole from, that would catch up to him. Which inevitably led to him pushing an elderly lady too hard, her head crushing against the brick wall… 

It might be because of all these crimes haunting him ever since that day, that he now finds himself in front of a church. Rain flowing down, he looks over the building, remembering how he never paid much attention to churches, but right now it somehow looks more daunting than a squad of patrolling soldiers. 

He steps inside, as the warm lighting illuminates everything in a way that makes Sergey forget about that daunting feeling. Water dripping down from him step after step, he makes his way further in, drawn in by a voice that sounded calm, yet firm. Unable to look that priest straight in the face, he waited until he finished giving a speech, and stepped up to him. He gathered courage to look at the priest, and dropped to his knees - it was the Patriarch himself! The very same Patriarch that was now worriedly looking over him - “What is wrong, my child? Can I help you?” Sergey felt a lump in his throat, flapping his mouth uselessly for a moment, then finally speaking: “...I need to know, please tell me Father, can I, someone who crossed the line, ever repent for the things I’ve done?”

options.name: Pavlov’s expression was much like his voice, - “The Lord guided you here for many reasons. Repentance might just be one of them. We will help you.”

title: Repenting From Hereticism
desc:
Reporting from the border regions of the Army of Saint George, it is with great joy that we announce the news of the Tatar conversion to Christianity. In a stunning development, the Tatar community in the region has embraced the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ. 

As tensions have risen between the Our Holy State and the Tatar minority, a blessed turn of events has taken place. Members of the Tatar community have begun converting to Christianity, prompting the attention of Mikhail Antipin. 

Antipin has praised the Tatars who have embraced the faith. He sees their conversion as a positive step towards unity and has lauded them with praise. 

In a recent address to the nation, Antipin announced that the Tatars who convert to Christianity will be rewarded for their faith. They will receive a tax exemption and be granted access to the same opportunities as Orthodox Christians within the state. 

The Army of St. George has also begun a campaign to promote Christianity within the Tatar community, sending missionaries to mosques and community centres to spread the faith. This move has received mixed reactions from the Tatar community, with some embracing the new faith and others vehemently opposing it. In time of course, all will accept the true teachings of our Lord and Saviour. 

Despite the backlash, Antipin remains committed to promoting unity and the true religion within Russia. He believes that by embracing Christianity, the Tatars will become a vital part of the country's future and will be able to contribute to its growth and prosperity. 

Only time will tell how this development will shape the future of the Tatar community within Russia. However, one thing is certain:

title: Quotas For Everything
desc:
Artyom remembered when he used to work at an old Soviet munitions factory in Gorky. Back in Gorky, he helped make the shells that Soviet T-34 Tanks needed to blast the Nazi scumbags into nothing more than bones and tattered remnants of uniforms. At the factory, he had to meet a quota every day. A quota on the amount of shells he needed to make. He met that quota every day, for he knew that if he didn’t, he would just be another roadblock to Russian Victory. Yet despite his best efforts, Russia fell and even though he met every single quota he was given, he still felt like he let his country down. 

Now Artyom is working at a truck assembly plant in Vyatka. Artyom doesn't help make the trucks himself, he’s too old for that, but he does help organise the plant’s paperwork. He helps figure out delivery timetables, when trucks can get off the line and when materials to make new ones are coming in. It’s quite different from working at a massive munitions factory, but the one thing that’s stayed the same since he went back to work assembling the critical resources for the Patriarch’s Reunification of Russia, is the quotas. The most important quota for the plant is for the trucks of course, but there are quotas all up and down the supply chain. Quotas for the trucks windscreens, quotas for the trucks wheels and quotas for the trucks engine.  

But they’re not the only quotas. The coal power plant that generates the electricity for the plant has a quota on the power it produces. The farms that grow wheat to make the plant workers lunch have a quota on the amount of wheat they have to grow. Hell, the papermakers that make the paper Artyom uses to fill out his quotas also have quotas to follow. Alot has changed since Artyom returned to the factories, but in some ways it's still the same.

title: The Holiday Comes To Us
desc:
On the outskirts of Vyatka, near the now-famous “Vyatka Vodka” distillery, a new building had finished construction today. Seemingly just an extension of the distillery, it was actually a completely separate factory, although it was also producing an addicting drink, much like its neighbor. 

Stepping out of a black sedan, which was very clearly imported from OFN, two men in suits dirtied their leather shoes with the cold Russian soil. Not too bothered by it however, they rapidly approached the foreman at the gate of this factory, who was accompanied by none other than the Patriarch himself. He was positively gleaming with excitement as the two foreigners approached, even exclaiming: “Welcome, dear friends!” in a heavily accented English as they came close, and personally shook hands with both of them. It looked kind of surreal, with them standing in front of a big red sign with “Coca-Cola” written on it. 

One of the men spoke in English, after he was finished the second person interpreted everything in Russian: they thanked the Patriarch for the welcome, although it wasn’t exactly a prestigious one, and asked if the factory was finished. They needed to know this because advertisements needed to start being produced and relayed over the radio all across Russia, and they needed to settle on a catchy tune, for which Izvekov’s personal opinion would be counted, being the one who proposed this foreign business expansion in the first place. Although Izvekov wasn’t too well versed in song writing, he did feel the chilly winds of late autumn, signaling the approaching New Years. “How about this,” - he raised his finger after a moment, and started to hum the tune: 

“...Hmmmm Hm-hm Hm-hm, Hmmmm Hm-Hm Hm-Hm… …The Holiday comes to us, The Holiday comes to us,... It brings joy and an invigorating taste, The Holiday always has a Real taste!”

options.name: Everyone but Izvekov noticed that he rhymed taste with taste. At least the tune was nice.

title: A Good Time
desc:
Fyodor Petrovich could not exactly be described as a spendthrift. He earned to provide for his family, and only just enough to save a little each month, which made Fyodor, and especially his wife Ulyana, extremely careful with their money. A good quality to have in a family, it however slowly made their children - Igor and Natasha, sadder by the day, having been denied sweets and toys for the last year, the very same sweets and toys they constantly see proudly paraded around by the kids of richer parents. 

Fyodor felt for his kids, remembering how in his youth he himself envied neighborhood kids with toys. Flipping through the papers one Friday morning, he came across something incredibly intriguing: “COME ONE, COME ALL, To the grand opening of Vyatka Mall!” The description of this place made it out to be like it is a superior supermarket, which sounds simply unbelievable! How can one place be this convenient in every single way? There was even a food court in there- “Wait. That’s it!” - Fyodor thought, and began making preparations for the weekend. 

As if no time had passed, the family now found themselves in front of the giant building, with a big sign on its wall: “Garden of Eden”. Guiding the stunned family members, Fyodor took them inside, which only made the stun worse. Their eyes simply didn’t know where to stop. Getting a hold of himself, Fyodor asked a passerby directions to the food court, who shrugged it off and pointed to a tall board - “There’s a map you oaf, follow it.”, and left in a hurry. It wasn’t long until they arrived there, and truly lived up to its name - a large court, surrounded by food stalls large enough to be small restaurants. Having to pick for the family, as they were out of it, Fyodor walked up to the one with two golden arches above it.

title: Food for the Hungry, Clothes for the Cold
desc:
Where the once-mighty Russian nation lay in ruins, its people suffered in the depths of despair as self-centred warlords tore apart the Russian scraps for themselves. Whilst Antipin and the Order of Saint George might be seen as just another Warlord with a Hardcore Religious Twist, but for many Russians under their influence, they are more than just another warlord. To them, Patriarch Peter II is a beacon of hope. Clad in his humble black cassock, his eyes filled with unwavering determination, he dedicated himself to providing aid and solace to those who had lost everything.

Amidst the crumbling infrastructure and echoes of a once-thriving society, the Patriarch brought relief to those who had been left destitute. With dozens of small groups of devoted volunteers, they traversed the Kingdom of Christ, guided by the belief of helping those who follow God’s Path and Teachings (The Others can be dealt with by other means).

Carrying baskets laden with food and sacks filled with warm clothing, the groups helped the most vulnerable and poor to ensure they were able to live another day. They sought out families who huddled together in the remains of their homes, their faces etched with weariness and their eyes clouded with anguish.

Sometimes the Patriarch himself was able to attend and help out the volunteers to distribute the much-needed supplies. He offered words of comfort and solace, assuring them that they were not forgotten, the light of hope and fires of vengeance still flickered in their souls. His voice, filled with unwavering conviction, cut through the silence, inspiring a flicker of determination within the hearts of those he touched.

title: A Loyal Follower
desc:
Kazan never cared for Andrei. Ever since he entered the city with only the Red Army Uniform he was wearing, the city had left him to rot away. Forced to live on the streets and in the alleys, every day trying to find a way to survive. This was the same situation for years until the city was surrounded and overrun. Out were the Tatars asserting their independence, and in were the Religious Militants determined to reunify Russia under God’s Vision.

At the start, nothing changed, same old searching for food to live another day. Until one day, Andrei saw a soup kitchen open to those who were destitute like him, offering free hot food and drinks. Andrei did not hesitate, for the first time since he walked through the city gates, he was welcomed with open arms and had a full meal, a distant memory he had once forgotten. He started coming every day, and every day he would get his meal and sit near a Priest giving a sermon in the Kitchen. Andrei began to smile again, something he had not done in years.

The daily sermons began to change him, the priest was passionate, determined and loyal to God. He envisioned a Russia of God-fearing men ready to wipe out the German Scum sitting on their throne of Russian Skulls in Moscow. Andrei began to believe him and his vision. Before long he signed up to join the new Army that had occupied the city. The training was tough, even tougher than his old Red Army training, but it helped him turn into the Man he is now. He was loyal to God, loyal to Christ and loyal to Patriarch Peter II thanks to his training, and he would be forever loyal to the people who actually began to care for him.

title: A Radical Interpretation of the Bible
desc:
Like many things in life, the nearly 2 Millennium old Bible is often open to interpretation. Some see it as a vessel that calls for unity, humanity and support for everyone’s fellowman. Others see it as a pillar of old, holding up the Old Status Quo when people followed God and his Disciples. Then there are those who look at it in a far different light.

The man standing in front of the altar was one of those men. “The Popes of Rome may be Heretics, but that didn’t mean they always had bad ideas” Antipin boomed from his altar throughout the packed Church, full of people from the Highest of Religious officials to the Common Farmer. “In the year 1096, the Holy Land was occupied by a people who didn’t follow even a single Christian Teaching, and they were close to threatening Constantinople. The Entire Christian World was under threat, true believer or not.”

Antipin stayed silent, trying to claw his followers further into his sermon. “In the midst of this major threat, that same year, Pope Urban II made the decision to call a Crusade, to dismantle the Heretical Kingdoms that Threatened Christianity, to repeal the Anti-Christian and to retake the Holy Land and Jerusalem.”The Preachers looked as if they wanted to join the Crusade too, and luckily for them, Antipin would give them that choice. “Once we have brought back Russia from the ruins of the Bolsheviks, we shall start a new Crusade for Moscow, and then to Berlin. Deus Volt!” Antipin yelled as the entire room stood up and followed his lead in one large roar of the words that will lead the Russian Crusade…

title: A Toast to Our, and the Republic’s Health
desc:
Izvekov is a religious man, a man who has devoted his life to God, Christ and the Russian People. Izvekov is the Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church and leads the Orthodox Republic of Russia, a state where the light of democracy is led by the followers of God. Despite all that, it doesn't mean he can’t enjoy a nice drink of Vodka every now and then. He and Stalina had met up in his office to discuss the nation’s reindustrialisation, but they had soon moved on to talking about their personal lives over a few shots of vodka.

“Sergey, may I ask a question? Did you ever think you’d make it this far, becoming the Patriarch, leading a movement to reunite Russia under a Christian Democratic Republic?” Stalina asked him as she poured herself some more Vodka. “Of course” Ivekov responded in a flash. “Sure I wasn’t as influential as Antipin or Pavlov, but the most dangerous man in politics is the one who acts behind the scenes, in the dark, as a forgotten entity. I’m sure the political alleys of Komi have taught you that.”

Izvekov thought back to those early days. He was a Priest back then, an influential one within the Order, but not as high up as Pavlov or Antipin. He was only able to start exerting control once the Order had consolidated its holdings in Western Russia after he slowly made connections behind the scenes during the Second Smuta. “What about you Svetlana, did you see yourself as Prime Minister under me?” Izvekov asked her, flipping the question towards Stalina. “Well I always think I’d lead a Democratic Republic, but this is certainly quite different from Komi, and significantly more stable too.”

They both chuckled as they finished up their drinks for the night.

title: Deja Vu
desc:
Sergeant Dimitri had been through a lot during his years of service. First, he was a Red Army Drafttee pulled away from his family to fight the impending Nazi Army, then a WRRF Soldier determined to take back Moscow for Russia, then a demoralised deserter wandering the Siberian Wastes. He only began to recover when he met with the Order in Gayny, where they offered him a chance to reunify Russia not under Bukharin and Lenin, but instead under God and Christ.

As he observed his Platoon test out their firing skills on the range with the latest batch of firearms from Gorky, he cast his mind back to his early days in the Order’s “Army”. At the time, it was far from a traditional army, back then it was just ragtag groups of militant orthodox monks, former Red Army Veterans, and farmers who wished to protect their communities. How the Order has changed since then.

The Order’s Militia has formed into a proper Russian Army capable of bringing the remnants of free Russia together. The men have rifles produced in their own factories, rather than nabbing those off their fallen enemies, and actual uniforms so they can properly tell who’s on their side, resulting in a drop in friendly-fire incidents.

Oddly enough, it felt like he was back in the Red Army. The only difference was that back then he and his squad worshipped Communism, Marx, Lenin and Bukharin. Now his platform worships God, Christ and the Patriarch.

title: The Frozen Dock
desc:
In the frigid winter of northern Russia, where the relentless cold and biting winds seemed to constantly test the resilience of its inhabitants, Pavlov found himself overlooking the construction of a new dockyard near Arkhangelsk. Despite the harsh conditions of Russia’s frozen north, he was determined to visit the Order’s soon-to-be newest dockyard. If they were to establish a proper Russian Navy, it will greatly help legitimise them and make any attacks on the Eastern Warlords easier

Of course, the dockyard isn’t just for building and holding naval ships for the Order, it also holds the promise of economic growth and prosperity for the region, connecting remote villages to vital trade routes and opening doors to new opportunities in a region with barely any land connections, in some ways it was a situation where the Order can hit two birds with one stone.

With his thick coat tightly wrapped around him, Pavlov made his way through the snow-covered docks, offering words of encouragement and prayers to the labourers who toiled diligently day and night to establish a new hub of military and commerce. The workers, their faces hardened by the elements, found solace in the Patriarch's presence and his teachings to them, at a time when hope was hard to come by.

Father Pavlov blessed the dockyard in a solemn ceremony, invoking God's protection over the structure and all who would benefit from its existence, and its workers, praying for good health while they finish the port. The icy waters of the nearby river seemed to bow in reverence as the priest's words echoed through the air, promising a future of prosperity and hope in a region once lost to the elements after the once-mighty Soviet Union fell.

title: The Zealot Warrior
desc:
The Past decides the Future. That phrase had been stuck in Antipin’s head for days as he tried to read the book he had on his desk with only the slowly dimming candlelight offering assistance. He was attempting to read up on the First Crusade, where the Christain World united to evict the Muslims from the Holy Land. Both he and Pavlov agreed that a Russian Crusade was needed to bring the nation back together, but Pavlov wasn't willing to commit to the Crusade, not like he was prepared to.

He still respected Pavlov, he had brought his army together in the first place, but he simply wasn’t the man capable of leading the Crusade. The Crusades of Old were initially successful, but slowly over time they fell apart due to degeneracy, lack of faith and personal ambitions ahead of God. To ensure a continuous victory, all must remain loyal to God, and those who are not must to routed out of their holes of despair before they take the entire country with them and allow the Nazi jackboot to enter deeper into Russia.

Antipin had written to Pavlov about the need to ensure a God-Fearing Army, one devoted to God and Russia, one ready to give their lives to bring God’s reach over Siberia and one ready to ensure the continued sanctity of God’s Vision. Pavlov had never seen him the same way again. It was clear to him that he would soon be God’s Destined Servant to save Russia, but no matter how loyal and hardworking his followers may be, Pavlov still holds the Order’s Favour. One day he will become God’s Destined Servant to reunite Russia, for now, he will simply read into the past to prevent future mistakes.

title: The Saint, the Righteous, and the Damned
desc:
The once intricately sewn clothes of the false tsar were now mere rags, torn and covered in mud all over. It was not easy to be judged by the same people you’ve demanded submission from. Not when one of those people was Antipin.

Alas, it was not time to regret or dwell on your past choices. It was time to face their consequences.

Antipin was angrily stomping around the weak and frail body of the beaten up tsar, shouting, swearing, and most importantly, praying that he Vladimir may be damned by god for eternity. He did all this for good reason, however. Let’s not forget, the royal family abused all sorts of power, including the Church, and this was not about to happen again.

“Take a seat Mikhail-, we won’t be able to make any sort of proper level-headed judgement if you keep screaming about.” Pavlov spoke as his back was gently resting against the walls of Vladimir’s cell.

“Judgement?! What sort of judgement does this filth need? I regret even dragging his body to this decrepit chamber, and that says something about all this, Kirill, it says-” Before he had a chance to continue, Pavlov had already begun speaking again.

“It says that he will die an unfair death. He has sinned, yes, but so has everyone else, including yourself and I. Does that mean we will spare him judgement? No. But it does mean that he will be publicly judged rather than be killed like a coward here. We are a nation, Mikhail, not a clique or a gang of thugs. We do things in order.”

Antipin took in a deep breath hearing Pavlov’s reply. He knew he could not change his mind, whether he liked it or not. Why should he be mad anyways? He was going to be killed regardless... right?

title: The Empty Throne
desc:
Kirillovich surveyed out the palace window. His eyes felt heavy. He had tried to sleep but was too consumed in thoughts of his family. It had been days since he had proper contact with them; they were being held separate from him, maybe to make him desperate? He didn't know. These people had no love for his lineage. To them, God had smitten his family down for failing in their duties to him and, along with them, the people of Russia. Were they wrong?

His Uncle before him had neglected his title, using it as a means to accomplish little but his own personal enjoyment, and what about him?

The nephew of that man? The man who declared eternal friendship and cooperation with the Germans, who, even when he was off their leash during the West-Russian War, rallied collaborators and helped push the German offensive, and for what? A scrap of territory to call his kingdom in a ruined land, dealt by those he thought he could use to establish his rightful rule?

He ground his teeth, still trying to act as if he had composure even when nobody was around. 

His mind had trailed back to his family; what would happen to his wife, Leonida, or daughter? Would they treat them as the Bolsheviks had his Uncle's family, or simply just leave them in the ruins to die of starvation?

He leaned further toward the window and opened it. As he did, he noticed one of the armed guards sent by the Order staring up at him, his eyes slightly squinted, refusing to look away. Kirillovich huffed; it was almost comedic. They were watching his every move, not letting him escape their punishment, not that he thought he could anyway. He closed the window and slightly waved as if to say, "Yes, believe it or not, I'm still here." Then he backed away. At best, he was a traitor to them; at worst, he was a heathen. He just hoped that their judgment, "God's" judgment, didn't pass down to his loved ones. Just as he was about to lose himself again in his own thoughts, a knock came from his door. How formal, he'd honestly expected them just to barge through the door if they needed him. While he walked over to the door, Kirillovich structured himself; he at least wanted to appear like he was still collected. He reached one hand out and opened the door, and as he expected, one of the guards stood in front of him, looking at him as if he was inconvenienced just to be before him. 

"Vladimir, I have a message for you."

Kirilovich swallowed; this was it. Fate had finally arrived.

"What is it?

He just hoped that their judgment, "God's" judgment, didn't pass down to his loved ones. Just as he was about to lose himself again in his own thoughts, a knock came from his door. How formal, he'd honestly expected them just to barge through the door if they needed him. While he walked over to the door, Kirillovich structured himself; he at least wanted to appear like he was still collected. He reached one hand out and opened the door, and as he expected, one of the guards stood in front of him, looking at him as if he was inconvenienced just to be before him. 

"Vladimir, I have a message for you."

Kirilovich swallowed; this was it. Fate had finally arrived.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]A Nation United by God
desc:
Everyone knew that Russia would rise again, even if they didn`t say it out loud. It was only a matter of time before the nation rose again from the ashes to make the world tremble once more. But of all the possible contenders to reunite the country, this one was the least expected.

The inevitable has happed: Russia now stands as a united nation, only the people ruling it were different. The Orthodox Church now rules Russia for the first time in its history, with its Patriarch Kirill I as its head. Russia is now the first of its kind in the modern world. A state guided by God, the words and principles of the Bible now run the Russian machine, with its citizens loyal servants of the Church, religious minorities forced to convert, and political opposition and secularism a thing of the past. But whatever its ideology, it is now clear that the Russian bear has finally awakened from its long slumber, and the whole world will now see the true wrath and power of God as the bear's attention turns to the West.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]A Free and Holy Russia
desc:
The Russian Orthodox Church had never held a position of power before. Its existence was dedicated to serving the Tsar until the Communists attempted to destroy it. Nobody anticipated their ascent to power during the nation's darkest hour, yet now Eurasia quakes as they have emerged.

For the first time in 30 years, Russia stands united, now under the rule of Pimen I, the Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church, who has introduced a new kind of democracy unseen across the world. A democracy guided by the wisdom of God, with all political parties, from the left to the right, supporting Christian theology. Already, new elections are have been slated next year, with former secular politicians joining ranks and running for the country's newly formed parliament and prime minister posts. Such a system has gained a few followers back home, though it is only limited. And with the Patriarch having announced plans to reclaim forner Russian land, it is obvious now to all, that the world has entered a new age, and it will never be the same again.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Orthodoxy in Latin America
desc: In the hills and ravines of Mexico, people go to their local church every Sunday to get themselves closer to God, and to find solace in their lives. It is a generational practice that most Mexicans have been doing for all their lives, but recently, a new form of the Christian cross is becoming well known amongst the population. Both in the cities and the villages all across the nation, an burgeoning Orthodox community is rising across all social classes. Where the Catholic Church has long been seen as a corrupt, reactionary instrument of PRI rule, the Orthodox priests there, coming from the Russian Anarchy, have helped out ordinary citizens and done charitable acts for the needy members of society, which has resulted in the increasing popularity of the church. In response to such events, the Catholic Church has undergone their own social program to boost popularity amongst the Mexican public, yet the Orthodox Church is set to become a new religious force in the nation, with 5% of the population expected to become Orthodox Christians by the end of this decade.
